bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑第237巻

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 237.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 237.

sentences.zh: 【唐紀五十三】起柔兆閹茂，盡屠維赤奮若六月，凡三年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 53], from Rouzhao Yanmao through the sixth month of Tuvi Chifenruo, altogether a little more than three years.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Records 53, from the yiyou year (805) through the sixth month of the wuzi year (808)—a span of a little more than three years.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丙寅朔，上帥群臣詣興慶宮上上皇尊號。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day bingyin, the Emperor led the civil and military officials to Xingqing Palace to present the honorary title to the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the Emperor led his officials to Xingqing Palace to bestow an honorific title upon the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, he proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he declared a general amnesty and inaugurated a new reign era.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以鄂岳觀察使韓皋爲奉義節度使。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Han Gao, the E-Yue observation commissioner, was appointed military governor of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day, Han Gao was transferred from E-Yue observation commissioner to military governor of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，以奉義留後伊宥爲安州刺史兼安州留後。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Yi You, the acting commander of Fengyi, was made prefect of Anzhou and also acting commander of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, Yi You, who had been acting commander at Fengyi, was appointed prefect of Anzhou and left in charge there as acting commander.

sentences.zh: 宥，愼之子也。

translations.literal: You was the son of Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Yi You was a son of Yi Shen.

sentences.zh: 壬午，加成德節度使王士眞同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Wang Shizhen, military governor of Chengde, was additionally made co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Wang Shizhen of Chengde was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 甲申，上皇崩於興慶宮。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen, the Retired Emperor died at Xingqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiashen day, the Retired Emperor died at Xingqing Palace.

sentences.zh: 劉闢既得旌節，志益驕，求兼領三川，上不許。

translations.literal: Once Liu Pi had received the command banner and credentials, his ambition grew ever more arrogant; he asked to hold all three Shu circuits concurrently, and the Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Pi received his commission as military governor, he grew increasingly arrogant and asked to govern all three Shu circuits at once. The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 闢遂發兵圍東川節度使李康於梓州，欲以同幕盧文若爲東川節度使。

translations.literal: Pi thereupon raised troops and besieged Li Kang, military governor of Dongchuan, at Zizhou, intending to install his former staff colleague Lu Wenruo as military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Pi then mobilized his army and besieged Li Kang, the Dongchuan governor, at Zizhou, planning to install his former staff colleague Lu Wenruo as the new Dongchuan governor.

sentences.zh: 推官莆田林蘊力諫闢舉兵，辟怒，械繫於獄，引出，將斬之，陰戒行刑者使不殺，但數礪刃於其頸，欲使屈服而赦之。

translations.literal: The judicial aide Lin Yun of Putian strenuously remonstrated against Pi's raising troops. Pi was enraged, had him shackled and imprisoned, then brought him out to be executed. He secretly instructed the executioners not to kill him but only to whet the blade repeatedly against his neck, intending to make him submit so that he might then pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yun, a judicial aide from Putian, strongly urged Pi not to take up arms. Enraged, Pi had him shackled and thrown in prison, then led him out for execution. Secretly he told the executioners not to kill him but only to grind their blades against his neck again and again, hoping to break his will and then spare him.

sentences.zh: 蘊叱之曰：「豎子，當斬即斬，我頸豈汝砥石邪！」

translations.literal: Yun shouted at him, "You wretch—if you mean to cut off my head, then cut it off! Do you take my neck for your whetstone?"
translations.idiomatic: Yun shouted at him, "You cur—if you mean to kill me, then kill me! Is my neck your whetstone?"

sentences.zh: 闢顧左右曰：「眞忠烈之士也！」

translations.literal: Pi turned to those beside him and said, "A man of true loyalty and valor!"
translations.idiomatic: Pi turned to his attendants and said, "A man of true loyalty and valor!"

sentences.zh: 乃黜爲唐昌尉。

translations.literal: He then demoted him to be assistant magistrate of Tangchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then demoted Lin Yun to assistant magistrate of Tangchang.

sentences.zh: 上欲討闢而重於用兵，公卿議者亦以爲蜀險固難取，杜黃裳獨曰：「闢狂戇書生，取之如拾芥耳！

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to campaign against Pi but was reluctant to commit to war. The ministers who deliberated also held that Shu was rugged and strongly fortified and hard to take. Du Huangshang alone said, "Pi is a reckless, arrogant bookworm—taking him will be like picking up a mustard seed!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wanted to suppress Pi but hesitated to commit forces. Most ministers argued that Shu was rugged, well fortified, and hard to conquer. Du Huangshang alone said, "Pi is nothing but a reckless scholar—capturing him will be as easy as picking up a mustard seed!

sentences.zh: 臣知神策軍使髙崇文勇略可用，願陛下專以軍事委之，勿置監軍，辟必可擒。」

translations.literal: Your servant knows that Gao Chongwen, commissioner of the Shence Army, has courage and strategy that can be employed. I beg Your Majesty to entrust the military affairs to him alone and not appoint army supervisors; then Pi can certainly be captured."
translations.idiomatic: I know that Gao Chongwen of the Shence Army has both courage and strategy. Entrust the campaign entirely to him, Your Majesty, and do not appoint eunuch army supervisors—then Pi will surely be taken."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李吉甫亦勸上討蜀，上由是器之。

translations.literal: The Hanlin academician Li Jifu also urged the Emperor to campaign against Shu, and from this the Emperor came to value him.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Li Jifu likewise urged an expedition against Shu, and the Emperor thereafter held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 戊子，命左神策行營節度使髙崇文將歩騎五千爲前軍，神策京西行營兵馬使李元奕將歩騎二千爲次軍，與山南西道節度使嚴礪同討辟。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, he ordered Gao Chongwen, campaign commissioner of the Left Shence Army, to lead five thousand infantry and cavalry as the vanguard; Li Yuanyi, troop commander of the Shence Western Capital campaign force, to lead two thousand infantry and cavalry as the second echelon; and together with Yan Li, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, to campaign against Pi.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day he ordered Gao Chongwen of the Left Shence campaign force to lead five thousand foot and horse as the vanguard, Li Yuanyi of the Shence Western Capital detachment to lead two thousand as the second wave, and Yan Li of Shannan West to join them in suppressing Liu Pi.

sentences.zh: 時宿將名位素重者甚衆，皆自謂當征蜀之選，及詔用崇文，皆大驚。

translations.literal: At that time there were many veteran generals of long-standing fame and rank, all of whom considered themselves the ones who ought to be chosen for the Shu expedition. When the edict appointed Chongwen, all were greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior generals of high standing had assumed they would be chosen to lead the Shu campaign. When the edict named Gao Chongwen instead, they were all astonished.

sentences.zh: 上與杜黃裳論及籓鎭，黃裳曰：「德宗自經憂患，務爲姑息，不生除節帥。

translations.literal: The Emperor discussed frontier commands with Du Huangshang. Huangshang said, "Since Emperor Dezong suffered those trials, he devoted himself to indulgence and never removed a military governor while he still lived.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor discussed the frontier commands with Du Huangshang, Huangshang said, "After his own trials, Emperor Dezong pursued a policy of appeasement and never removed a living military governor.

sentences.zh: 有物故者，先遣中使察軍情所與則授之。

translations.literal: When one died, he first sent a palace envoy to observe which way army sentiment leaned, and then invested that man.
translations.idiomatic: When one died, he first sent a palace envoy to see whom the troops favored, then appointed that man.

sentences.zh: 中使或私受大將賂，歸而譽之，即降旄鉞，未嘗有出朝廷之意者。

translations.literal: Sometimes the envoy would privately accept bribes from a senior officer; on returning he would praise that man, and the command banner and battle-axe would be bestowed—never once with the intent coming from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes an envoy would take bribes from a senior officer, return to court praising him, and the commission would be granted—never once reflecting the court's own choice.

sentences.zh: 陛下必欲振舉綱紀，宜稍以法度裁製蕃鎭，則天下可得而理也。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty truly wishes to revive law and discipline, you should gradually restrain the frontier commands by statute and regulation; then all under Heaven can be brought to order."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty truly wishes to restore discipline, you should gradually bring the frontier commands under the law—and then the realm can be governed."

sentences.zh: 上深以爲然，於是始用兵討蜀，以至威行兩河，皆黃裳啓之也。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply agreed. From this he began to use troops against Shu, and extending to the time when his authority prevailed in the two He regions—all of this Huangshang had set in motion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor strongly agreed. From this came the campaign against Shu and, eventually, imperial authority restored in the two He regions—all of it set in motion by Huangshang.

sentences.zh: 髙崇文屯長武城，練卒五千，常如寇至，卯時受詔，辰時即行，器械糗糧，一無所闕。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen encamped at Changwu Fortress and drilled five thousand soldiers, always as though the enemy were at hand. He received an edict at the mao hour and marched at the chen hour; weapons, gear, and rations—nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen camped at Changwu and drilled five thousand men as though the enemy were always near. He would receive orders at dawn and march by mid-morning, with weapons, equipment, and provisions always complete.

sentences.zh: 甲午，崇文出斜谷，李元奕出駱谷，同趣梓州。

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, Chongwen marched out through Xiegu Pass and Li Yuanyi through Luogu Pass, both hurrying toward Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day, Chongwen advanced through Xiegu Pass and Li Yuanyi through Luogu Pass, both converging on Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇文軍至興元，軍士有食於逆旅，折人匕箸者，崇文斬之以徇。

translations.literal: When Chongwen's army reached Xingyuan, a soldier who ate at an inn and broke another man's spoon and chopsticks was beheaded by Chongwen as a public warning.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongwen's army reached Xingyuan, he executed a soldier who had broken another traveler's utensils at an inn, making an example of him.

sentences.zh: 劉闢陷梓州，執李康。

translations.literal: Liu Pi captured Zizhou and seized Li Kang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi took Zizhou and captured Li Kang.

sentences.zh: 二月，嚴礪拔劍州，斬其刺史文德昭。

translations.literal: In the second month, Yan Li captured Jianzhou and beheaded its prefect, Wen Dezhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Yan Li took Jianzhou and executed its prefect, Wen Dezhao.

sentences.zh: 奚王誨落可入朝。

translations.literal: The Xi king Huiluoke came to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi chieftain Huiluoke came to pay court.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以誨落可爲饒樂郡王，遣歸。

translations.literal: On the day dingyou, Huiluoke was made Prince of Raole Commandery and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingyou day, Huiluoke was created Prince of Raole and sent back to his people.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，加魏博節度使田季安同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day guichou, Tian Ji'an, military governor of Weibo, was additionally made co-director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On the guichou day, Tian Ji'an of Weibo was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上與宰相論：「自古帝王，或勤勞庶政，或端拱無爲，互有得失，何爲而可？」

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the Emperor discussed with the chief ministers: "From antiquity emperors have either toiled at the myriad affairs of government or sat in dignified repose practicing nonaction—each course has had its gains and losses. Which is the right way?"
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day the Emperor asked his chief ministers, "Since antiquity, some rulers have thrown themselves into governing every detail, while others have sat in dignified ease and practiced nonaction. Each approach has had its strengths and flaws. Which is the better way?"

sentences.zh: 杜黃裳對曰：「王者上承天地宗廟，下撫百姓四夷，夙夜憂勤，固不可自暇自逸。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang replied, "A king above receives Heaven and Earth and the ancestral temples; below he comforts the common people and the four barbarians. Morning and night he must be anxious and diligent—he certainly cannot indulge leisure and ease for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang replied, "A ruler stands between Heaven and Earth and the ancestral shrines above, and the people and the four quarters below. He must labor day and night with care; he cannot afford idleness or self-indulgence.

sentences.zh: 然上下有分，紀綱有敘，苟愼選天下賢才而委任之，有功則賞，有罪則刑，選用以公，賞刑以信，則誰不盡力，何求不獲哉！

translations.literal: Yet superior and subordinate have their divisions, and law and discipline have their order. If one carefully selects the worthy talents of all under Heaven and entrusts office to them—rewarding merit and punishing guilt, making selection by fairness and reward and punishment by trustworthiness—then who would not exert his utmost strength, and what sought goal would not be attained!
translations.idiomatic: Yet ruler and subject each have their proper place, and law and order have their sequence. If you carefully choose the ablest men in the realm and entrust them with office, rewarding merit and punishing fault with fairness and consistency, who would not give his all? What goal could fail to be reached?

sentences.zh: 明主勞於求人，而逸於任人，此虞舜所以能無爲而治者也。

translations.literal: An enlightened ruler toils at seeking men, yet is at ease in employing men—this is why Yu Shun was able to govern through nonaction.
translations.idiomatic: A wise ruler labors to find the right men, then rests easy in trusting them to their tasks—that is how Yu Shun governed through nonaction.

sentences.zh: 至於簿書獄市煩細之事，各有司存，非人主所宜親也。

translations.literal: As for the troublesome minutiae of ledgers, prisons, and markets, each has its responsible office; these are not what the ruler himself should attend to.
translations.idiomatic: As for the tedious details of accounts, courts, and markets, each has its proper office—the ruler should not handle them himself.

sentences.zh: 昔秦始皇以衡石程書，魏明帝自按行尚書事，隋文帝衞士傳餐，皆無補於當時，取譏於後來，其耳目形神非不勤且勞也，所務非其道也。

translations.literal: Formerly the First Emperor of Qin measured documents by the stone weight, Emperor Ming of Wei personally inspected the affairs of the Masters of Writing, and Emperor Wen of Sui had his guards pass meals along—all of this was of no benefit to their own times and drew ridicule from later ages. Their senses and spirits were not without diligence and toil; what they devoted themselves to was not the right path.
translations.idiomatic: The First Emperor of Qin weighed documents by the stone, Emperor Ming of Wei personally reviewed the Masters of Writing, and Emperor Wen of Sui had guards pass his meals to him—all useless in their day and mocked by posterity. They were not lacking in diligence, but they applied themselves to the wrong tasks.

sentences.zh: 夫人主患不推誠，人臣患不竭忠。

translations.literal: The trouble with rulers is not extending full sincerity; the trouble with ministers is not exhausting their loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's failing is unwillingness to trust fully; the minister's failing is unwillingness to serve loyally.

sentences.zh: 苟上疑其下，下欺其上，將以求理，不亦難乎！」

translations.literal: If the superior suspects his subordinates and subordinates deceive their superior, then to seek good order—will it not be difficult!"
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler distrusts his officials and officials deceive their ruler, how can good order be achieved?"

sentences.zh: 上深然其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 三月，丙寅，以神策京西行營節度使范希朝爲右金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day bingyin, Fan Xichao, campaign commissioner of the Shence Western Capital force, was made Grand General of the Right Golden Guards.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the bingyin day, Fan Xichao of the Shence Western Capital campaign was appointed Grand General of the Right Golden Guards.

sentences.zh: 髙崇文引兵自閬州趣梓州，劉闢將邢泚引兵遁去，崇文入屯梓州。

translations.literal: Gao Chongwen led his troops from Langzhou toward Zizhou. Liu Pi's general Xing Ci led his troops in flight, and Chongwen entered and encamped at Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen marched from Langzhou toward Zizhou. Liu Pi's general Xing Ci withdrew, and Chongwen occupied Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 闢歸李康於崇文以求自雪，崇文以康敗軍失守，斬之。

translations.literal: Pi returned Li Kang to Chongwen in hope of clearing himself. Chongwen, on the grounds that Kang had been defeated and lost his post, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi sent Li Kang back to Chongwen hoping to clear his own name. Chongwen executed Kang for having lost his army and his post.

sentences.zh: 丙子，嚴礪奏克梓州。

translations.literal: On the day bingzi, Yan Li memorialized that Zizhou had been taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingzi day, Yan Li reported the capture of Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，制削奪劉闢官爵。

translations.literal: On the day dingchou, an edict stripped Liu Pi of his offices and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day, an edict stripped Liu Pi of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 初，韓全義入朝，以其甥楊惠琳知夏綏留後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Han Quanyi came to court, he left his nephew Yang Huilin in charge as acting commander of Xia-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Han Quanyi came to court, he left his nephew Yang Huilin as acting commander at Xia-Sui.

sentences.zh: 杜黃裳以全義出征無功，驕蹇不遜，直令致仕，以右驍衞將軍李演爲夏綏節度使。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang, on the grounds that Quanyi had campaigned without achievement and was arrogant and insubordinate, had him retire directly and appointed Li Yan, general of the Right Valiant Guards, military governor of Xia-Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang, citing Quanyi's failed campaigns and arrogant defiance, had him retire at once and appointed Li Yan of the Right Valiant Guards as military governor of Xia-Sui.

sentences.zh: 惠琳勒兵拒之，表稱「將士逼臣爲節度使」。

translations.literal: Huilin mobilized troops to resist and in a memorial stated, "The officers and soldiers have compelled your servant to become military governor."
translations.idiomatic: Huilin mobilized his troops to resist and memorialized that "the officers and men have forced me to become military governor."

sentences.zh: 河東節度使嚴綬表請討之。

translations.literal: Yan Shou, military governor of Hedong, memorialized requesting a campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shou of Hedong memorialized asking permission to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 詔河東、天德軍合撃惠琳，綬遣牙將阿跌光進及弟光顏將兵赴之，光進本出河曲歩落稽，兄弟在河東軍皆以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Hedong and the Tiande Army to strike Huilin jointly. Shou sent his adjutant Adie Guangjin and his younger brother Guangyan to lead troops thither. Guangjin was originally from the Buluoji tribe of the Yellow River bend; the brothers were both famed in the Hedong army for courage.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered Hedong and the Tiande Army to attack Huilin together. Shou sent his adjutant Adie Guangjin and his brother Guangyan with troops. Guangjin was from the Buluoji people of the Yellow River bend; both brothers were renowned in Hedong for bravery.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，夏州兵馬使張承金斬惠琳，傳首京師。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Zhang Chengjin, troop commander of Xiazhou, beheaded Huilin and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day, Zhang Chengjin of Xiazhou killed Huilin and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使韋丹至漢中，表言「髙崇文客軍遠鬥，無所資。

translations.literal: Wei Dan, military governor of Dongchuan, reached Hanzhong and memorialized, "Gao Chongwen's guest army fights far from home and has nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dan of Dongchuan reached Hanzhong and wrote, "Gao Chongwen's expeditionary force is fighting far from home without local support.

sentences.zh: 若與梓州，綴其士心，必能有功。」

translations.literal: If Zizhou is given to him, it will steady the hearts of his soldiers, and he will surely achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: If he is given Zizhou, it will steady his men's morale and he will surely succeed."

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，丁酉，以崇文爲東川節度副使、知節度事。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day dingyou, Chongwen was made vice military governor of Dongchuan and acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, on the dingyou day of the fourth month, Chongwen was made vice governor of Dongchuan with acting authority over the circuit.

sentences.zh: 潘孟陽所至，專事游宴，從僕三百人，多納賄賂。

translations.literal: Wherever Pan Mengyang went, he devoted himself solely to touring and feasting, with three hundred attendants, and accepted many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Pan Mengyang served, he devoted himself to pleasure and feasting, kept three hundred attendants, and accepted many bribes.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，甲辰，以孟陽爲大理卿，罷其度支、鹽鐵轉運副使。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard of this, on the day jiachen he made Mengyang Minister of Justice and removed him from his posts as vice commissioner of revenue and salt-iron transport.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor learned of this, on the jiachen day he transferred Mengyang to the Ministry of Justice and removed him from his finance and transport posts.

sentences.zh: 丙午，策試制舉之士，於是校書郎元稹、監察御史獨孤郁、校書郎下邽白居易、前進士蕭俛、沈傳師出焉。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, the palace examination was held for candidates of the special decree category. Those who passed were the proofreader Yuan Zhen, the investigating censor Dugu Yu, the proofreader Bai Juyi of Xia Gui, and the former presented scholars Xiao Mian and Shen Chuanshi.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day the palace examination was held for decree examination candidates. Those who passed included Yuan Zhen, Dugu Yu, Bai Juyi of Xia Gui, Xiao Mian, and Shen Chuanshi.

sentences.zh: 郁，及之子；

translations.literal: Yu was the son of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Yu was a son of Dugu Ji.

sentences.zh: 俛，華之孫；

translations.literal: Mian was the grandson of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Mian was a grandson of Xiao Hua.

sentences.zh: 傳師，既濟之子也。

translations.literal: Chuanshi was the son of Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Chuanshi was a son of Shen Jiji.

sentences.zh: 杜佑請解財賦之職，仍舉兵部侍郎、度支使、鹽鐵轉運副使李巽自代。

translations.literal: Du You asked to be relieved of his fiscal duties and recommended Li Xun, vice minister of war, revenue commissioner, and vice commissioner of salt-iron transport, to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Du You asked to step down from fiscal affairs and recommended Li Xun, who held the war ministry and finance posts, as his successor.

sentences.zh: 丁未，加佑司徒，罷其鹽鐵轉運使，以巽爲度支、鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: On the day dingwei, You was additionally made Minister of Education and removed as salt-iron transport commissioner; Xun was made revenue commissioner and salt-iron transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, Du You was made Minister of Education and relieved of the transport commission; Li Xun was appointed revenue and salt-iron commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自劉晏之後，居財賦之職者，莫能繼之。

translations.literal: From the time of Liu Yan onward, none who held the fiscal offices had been able to match him.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Yan's day, no one in charge of state finances had equaled him.

sentences.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬緡。

translations.literal: In one year under Xun's administration, tax revenues collected were about as great as Yan's highest; the next year they surpassed that, and in the year after that they increased by 1.8 million strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Xun's first year, tax receipts nearly matched Yan's best year; the next year they exceeded it, and the year after that rose by another 1.8 million strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 戊申，加隴右經略使、秦州刺史劉澭保義軍節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wushen, Liu Huan, frontier commissioner of Longyou and prefect of Qinzhou, was additionally made military governor of the Baoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day, Liu Huan of Longyou and Qinzhou was also appointed military governor of the Baoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，以元稹爲右拾遺，獨孤郁爲左拾遺，白居易爲盩厔尉、集賢校理，蕭俛爲右拾遺，沈傳師爲校書郎。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou, Yuan Zhen was made Remonstrator of the Right; Dugu Yu, Remonstrator of the Left; Bai Juyi, magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies; Xiao Mian, Remonstrator of the Right; and Shen Chuanshi, proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinyou day, Yuan Zhen was appointed Remonstrator of the Right, Dugu Yu Remonstrator of the Left, Bai Juyi magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Xiao Mian Remonstrator of the Right, and Shen Chuanshi proofreader.

sentences.zh: 稹上疎論諫職，以爲：「昔太宗以王珪、魏徴爲諫官，宴游寢食未嘗不在左右，又命三品以上入議大政，必遣諫官一人隨之，以參得失，故天下大理。

translations.literal: Zhen submitted a memorial discussing the remonstrance office, stating: "Formerly Emperor Taizong appointed Wang Gui and Wei Zheng as remonstrance officials; at banquets, excursions, sleep, and meals they were never absent from his side. He also ordered officials of the third rank and above who entered to deliberate great affairs of state to be accompanied by one remonstrance official, to take part in weighing gains and losses—therefore all under Heaven was well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen submitted a memorial on the remonstrance office. He wrote, "Emperor Taizong once appointed Wang Gui and Wei Zheng as remonstrators; they were at his side at meals, on excursions, even at rest. When officials of the third rank or higher came to discuss major policy, a remonstrator always accompanied them to weigh right and wrong. That is why the realm was well governed.

sentences.zh: 今之諫官，大不得豫召見，次不得參時政，排行就列，朝謁而已。

translations.literal: Today's remonstrance officials for the most part may not be summoned to audience; next they may not take part in current policy. They line up in their places and perform court obeisance—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Today's remonstrators are rarely summoned to audience and never take part in current policy. They simply line up for court and perform obeisance—that is all.

sentences.zh: 近年以來，正牙不奏事，庶官罷巡對，諫官能舉職者，獨誥命有不便則上封事耳。

translations.literal: In recent years the regular court session no longer hears memorials; junior officials no longer have rotating audiences. The only way remonstrance officials who can perform their duties do so is when an edict appointment is inconvenient—they submit a sealed memorial.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the regular court no longer hears business, and junior officials no longer have rotating audiences. Remonstrators who still perform their duty can do so only by submitting sealed memorials when an edict appointment seems wrong.

sentences.zh: 君臣之際，諷諭於未形，籌畫於至密，尚不能回至尊之盛意，況於既行之誥令，已命之除授，而欲以咫尺之書收絲綸之詔，誠亦難矣。

translations.literal: Between ruler and minister, to admonish when trouble has not yet taken shape and to plan at the most secret stage—even then one still cannot turn back the sovereign's settled intent. How much more when an edict has already been promulgated and an appointment already ordered—to hope to recall the imperial decree with a brief letter is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Between ruler and minister, even admonition at the earliest stage and counsel in the closest confidence often cannot change the sovereign's mind. How much harder when an edict has already gone forth and an appointment already made—to recall it with a short memorial is nearly impossible.

sentences.zh: 願陛下時於延英召對，使盡所懷，豈可置於其位而屛棄疎賤之哉！」

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty from time to time to summon us for audience in the Yanying Hall and let us express all that is in our hearts. How can you place us in office only to set us aside in neglect and contempt!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to summon us regularly to audience in the Yanying Hall and let us speak our minds fully. How can you give us office only to ignore and marginalize us?"

sentences.zh: 頃之，復上疎，以爲：「理亂之始，必有萌象。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he again submitted a memorial, stating: "At the beginning of order or disorder there are always early signs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he submitted another memorial: "At the outset of order or chaos there are always early signs.

sentences.zh: 開直言，廣視聽，理之萌也；

translations.literal: Opening the way for blunt speech and broadening what one sees and hears—these are the sprouts of order;
translations.idiomatic: Encouraging frank speech and broadening what the ruler sees and hears—these are signs of order;

sentences.zh: 甘諂諛，蔽近習，亂之象也。

translations.literal: delighting in flattery, shutting out close favorites—these are the signs of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: indulging flattery and shutting out honest counsel—these are signs of disorder.

sentences.zh: 自古人主即位之初，必有敢言之士，人主苟受而賞之，則君子樂行其道，競爲忠讜；

translations.literal: From antiquity, at the beginning of a ruler's accession there have always been men daring to speak. If the ruler accepts and rewards them, then gentlemen delight to practice their Way and vie in loyal frankness;
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, new rulers have always attracted men willing to speak boldly. If the ruler welcomes and rewards them, gentlemen gladly serve with integrity and compete in honest counsel;

sentences.zh: 小人亦貪其利，不爲回邪矣。

translations.literal: petty men also covet the profit and no longer practice crooked depravity.
translations.idiomatic: and even petty men, seeing the reward, cease their crooked ways.

sentences.zh: 如是，則上下之志通，幽遠之情達，欲無理得乎！

translations.literal: If it is so, then the intents of above and below are connected and the feelings of the distant and obscure reach through—how could one fail to attain order!
translations.idiomatic: Then the ruler and his officials understand one another, and even distant grievances are heard—how could order fail to follow!

sentences.zh: 苟拒而罪之，則君子巻懷括囊以保其身，小人阿意迎合以竊其位矣。

translations.literal: If one rejects and punishes them, then gentlemen roll up their principles and tie their mouths to preserve themselves, while petty men fawn and conform to steal their posts.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler rejects and punishes them, gentlemen withdraw and hold their tongues to save themselves, while petty men flatter their way into office.

sentences.zh: 如是，則十歩之事，皆可欺也，欲無亂得乎！

translations.literal: If it is so, then affairs ten paces away can all be deceived—how could one fail to fall into disorder!
translations.idiomatic: Then even matters ten paces away can be concealed from the throne—how could chaos fail to follow!

sentences.zh: 昔太宗初即政，孫伏伽以小事諫，太宗喜，厚賞之。

translations.literal: Formerly when Taizong had just taken power, Sun Fugai remonstrated over a small matter. Taizong was pleased and richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong first took the throne, Sun Fugai remonstrated over a minor matter. Taizong was pleased and rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 故當是時，言事者惟患不深切，未嘗以觸忌諱爲憂也。

translations.literal: Therefore at that time those who spoke on affairs only feared not being penetrating enough and never worried about touching taboos.
translations.idiomatic: At that time memorialists worried only that they had not spoken forcefully enough; they never feared giving offense.

sentences.zh: 太宗豈好逆意而惡從欲哉？

translations.literal: Did Taizong love what went against his wishes and hate what followed his desires?
translations.idiomatic: Did Taizong prefer opposition to agreement?

sentences.zh: 誠以順適之快小，而危亡之禍大故也。

translations.literal: Truly it was because the pleasure of compliance is small, while the calamity of peril and ruin is great.
translations.idiomatic: No—because the pleasure of having one's way is small, while the disaster of ruin is great.

sentences.zh: 陛下踐祚，今已週歳，夫聞有受伏伽之賞者。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has ascended the throne, and it is now a full year—yet has one heard of anyone receiving a reward like Sun Fugai's?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has reigned for a full year now, yet who has heard of anyone rewarded as Sun Fugai was?

sentences.zh: 臣等備位諫列，曠日彌年，不得召見，毎就列位，屛氣鞠躬，不敢仰視，又安暇議得失，獻可否哉！

translations.literal: We who fill the remonstrance ranks go day after day and year after year without being summoned to audience. Each time we take our places in line we hold our breath and bow, not daring to look up—how then could we find leisure to discuss right and wrong and offer approval or disapproval!
translations.idiomatic: We remonstrators have held our posts for years without a single audience. At court we hold our breath, bow, and dare not look up—how can we discuss policy or offer counsel?

sentences.zh: 供奉官尚爾，況疎遠之臣乎！

translations.literal: If even palace attendants are treated thus, how much more officials far removed!
translations.idiomatic: If even palace attendants fare so poorly, what of officials far from the throne!

sentences.zh: 此蓋群下因循之罪也。」

translations.literal: This is surely the fault of your subordinates' routine inertia."
translations.idiomatic: This is the fault of your officials' inertia."

sentences.zh: 因條奏請次對百官、復正牙奏事、禁非時貢獻等十事。

translations.literal: He thereupon submitted in detail ten requests, including rotating audiences for all officials, restoring memorials at the regular court session, and prohibiting untimely tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed ten recommendations, including rotating audiences for officials, restoring regular court memorials, and banning untimely tribute.

sentences.zh: 稹又以貞元中王伾、王叔文伎術得幸東宮，永貞之際幾亂天下，上書勸上早擇修正之士使輔導諸子，以爲：「太宗自爲蕃王，與文學淸修之士十八人居。

translations.literal: Zhen also cited how in the Zhenyuan era Wang Pi and Wang Shuwen, through technical arts, won favor in the Eastern Palace, and at the Yongzhen transition nearly threw all under Heaven into disorder. He submitted a memorial urging the Emperor early to choose upright cultivated scholars to instruct and guide the imperial sons, stating: "When Taizong was himself a frontier prince, he dwelt with eighteen men of literary learning and pure cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also cited Wang Pi and Wang Shuwen, who during the Zhenyuan era won favor in the Eastern Palace through their skills and nearly threw the realm into chaos at the Yongzhen transition. He urged the Emperor to choose upright scholars early to guide the princes, writing, "When Taizong was a frontier prince, he lived with eighteen men of learning and moral cultivation.

sentences.zh: 後代太子、諸王，雖有僚屬，日益疎賤，至於師傅之官，非眊聵廢疾不任事者，則休戎罷帥不知書者爲之。

translations.literal: In later generations, though the Heir Apparent and imperial princes had staff, these grew daily more remote and mean. As for the office of tutor, unless it was the dim-eyed, deaf, disabled, and unfit for duty, it was retired soldiers and dismissed commanders who could not read who held it.
translations.idiomatic: Later princes and heirs had staffs in name, but these posts grew ever more contemptible. Tutors were either the infirm and unfit for office, or retired soldiers and dismissed generals who could not read.

sentences.zh: 其友諭贊議之徒，尤爲冗散之甚，搢紳皆恥由之。

translations.literal: The companions, advisers, and commentators were especially superfluous and scattered; the gentry were all ashamed to take such posts.
translations.idiomatic: The companions and advisers were even more useless and contemptible; gentlemen of standing were ashamed to hold such posts.

sentences.zh: 就使時得僻老儒生，越月逾時，僅獲一見，又何暇傅之德義，納之法度哉！

translations.literal: Even if from time to time some obscure old Confucian scholar was obtained, after months and seasons he might gain a single audience—how then could there be leisure to transmit virtue and righteousness or instill law and measure!
translations.idiomatic: Even when some obscure old scholar was found, months might pass before he saw the prince once—how could he teach virtue or instill discipline?

sentences.zh: 夫以匹士愛其子，猶知求明哲之師而教之，況萬乘之嗣，系四海之命乎！」

translations.literal: If even a common gentleman who loves his son knows to seek a wise and enlightened teacher to instruct him, how much more the heir of ten thousand chariots, on whom the fate of all within the four seas depends!"
translations.idiomatic: If a common man who loves his son seeks a wise teacher for him, how much more should the heir to the throne, on whom the fate of the realm depends!"

sentences.zh: 上頗嘉納其言，時召見之。

translations.literal: The Emperor greatly approved and accepted his words and from time to time summoned him to audience.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor greatly approved his counsel and began to summon him to audience from time to time.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，邵王約薨。

translations.literal: On the day renxu, Prince Shao Yue died.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day, Prince Shao Yue died.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙子，以橫海留後程執恭爲節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the day bingzi, Cheng Zhigong, acting commander of Henghai, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the bingzi day, Cheng Zhigong, acting commander of Henghai, was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，尚書左丞、同平章事鄭餘慶罷爲太子賓客。

translations.literal: On the day gengchen, Zheng Yuqing, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing and co-director of the Secretariat, was removed and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day, Grand Councilor Zheng Yuqing was removed from office and made Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，尊太上皇后爲皇太后。

translations.literal: On the day xinmao, the Retired Empress was honored as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day, the Retired Empress was elevated to Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 劉闢城鹿頭關，連八柵，屯兵萬餘人以拒髙崇文。

translations.literal: Liu Pi fortified Lutou Pass, connected eight palisades, and stationed more than ten thousand troops to resist Gao Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi fortified Lutou Pass, linked eight stockades in a chain, and garrisoned more than ten thousand men to hold Gao Chongwen at bay.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁酉，崇文撃敗之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the day dingyou, Chongwen attacked and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the dingyou day, Gao Chongwen routed the rebel force.

sentences.zh: 闢置柵於關東萬勝堆。

translations.literal: Pi established palisades at Wansheng Mound east of the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi then threw up new stockades at Wansheng Mound, east of the pass.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，崇文遣驍將范陽髙霞寓攻奪之，下瞰關城，凡八戰皆捷。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Chongwen sent his fierce general Gao Xiayu of Fanyang to attack and seize it; overlooking the pass city from above, in eight battles all were victorious.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, Chongwen sent his crack general Gao Xiayu of Fanyang to storm the position; from the heights above they looked down on the pass fortress, and in eight engagements won every fight.

sentences.zh: 加盧龍節度使劉濟兼侍中。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, military governor of Lulong, was additionally made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, military governor of Lulong, was also appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 己亥，加平盧節度使李師古兼侍中。

translations.literal: On the day jihai, Li Shigu, military governor of Pinglu, was additionally made Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai day, Li Shigu of Pinglu was also made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 庚子，髙崇文破劉闢於德陽。

translations.literal: On the day gengzi, Gao Chongwen defeated Liu Pi at Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day, Gao Chongwen broke Liu Pi's army at Deyang.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，又破之於漢州。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, he again defeated them at Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day, he defeated them again at Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嚴礪遣其將嚴秦破闢衆萬餘人於綿州石碑谷。

translations.literal: Yan Li sent his general Yan Qin to defeat more than ten thousand of Pi's forces at Shibei Valley in Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Li dispatched his general Yan Qin, who routed more than ten thousand of Liu Pi's men at Shibei Valley in Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，李師古有異母弟曰師道，常疎斥在外，不免貧窶。

translations.literal: Initially, Li Shigu had a younger half-brother named Shidao, whom he often kept at a distance in exile, unable to escape poverty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shigu had a younger half-brother named Shidao whom he habitually kept at arm's length in the provinces, leaving him in no small poverty.

sentences.zh: 師古私謂所親曰：「吾非不友於師道也，吾年十五擁節旄，自恨不知稼穡之艱難。

translations.literal: Shigu privately said to his intimates: "It is not that I am unfriendly toward Shidao. At fifteen I wielded the command banner, and I regret not knowing the hardships of farming.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu confided to those close to him: "It is not that I bear ill will toward Shidao. I took up the command banner at fifteen and regret that I never learned how hard it is to earn one's bread from the soil.

sentences.zh: 況師道復減吾數歳，吾欲使之知衣食之所自來，且以州縣之務付之，計諸公必不察也。」

translations.literal: Moreover Shidao is several years younger than I. I wish to make him know where food and clothing come from, and to entrust him with prefectural and county affairs—calculating that you gentlemen will surely not notice."
translations.idiomatic: Shidao is several years my junior besides. I mean to teach him where food and clothing come from and put the routine business of prefectures and counties in his hands—you gentlemen, I expect, will not see through the design."

sentences.zh: 及師古疾篤，師道時知密州事，好畫及觱篥。

translations.literal: When Shigu's illness became critical, Shidao was then administering Mizhou, fond of painting and the bili pipe.
translations.idiomatic: When Shigu's illness turned grave, Shidao was serving as administrator of Mizhou and occupied himself with painting and the bili pipe.

sentences.zh: 師古謂判官髙沐、李公度曰：「迨吾之未亂也，欲有問於子。

translations.literal: Shigu said to the judicial aides Gao Mu and Li Gongdu: "Before my mind grows confused, I wish to ask you something.
translations.idiomatic: Shigu said to his aides Gao Mu and Li Gongdu: "While my mind is still clear, I want to put a question to you.

sentences.zh: 我死，子欲奉誰爲帥乎！」

translations.literal: When I die, whom do you wish to install as commander?"
translations.idiomatic: When I am gone, whom will you install as commander?"

sentences.zh: 二人相顧未對。

translations.literal: The two looked at each other and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: The two exchanged glances and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 師古曰：「豈非師道乎？

translations.literal: Shigu said: "Is it not Shidao?
translations.idiomatic: Shigu said, "Surely you mean Shidao?

sentences.zh: 人情誰肯薄骨肉而厚他人，顧置帥不善，則非徒敗軍政也，且覆吾族。

translations.literal: In human sentiment, who would treat flesh and blood thinly and outsiders thickly? But if the commander installed is unworthy, it will not merely ruin military and government affairs—it will also destroy our clan.
translations.idiomatic: Who, after all, would slight his own kin to favor an outsider? Yet if the wrong man is made commander, he will ruin not only the army and the administration but bring our whole house to ruin.

sentences.zh: 師道爲公侯子孫，不務訓兵理人，專習小人賤事以爲己能，果堪爲帥乎？

translations.literal: Shidao, as the descendant of a duke and marquis, does not pursue drilling troops and governing people, but devotes himself to petty vulgar pursuits as his own talent—is he truly fit to be commander?
translations.idiomatic: Shidao is the scion of a ducal house, yet he trains neither troops nor men and fancies himself skilled only in trifling, vulgar pastimes—is he really fit to command?

sentences.zh: 幸諸公審圖之！」

translations.literal: I hope you gentlemen will consider this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: I beg you to weigh this carefully!"

sentences.zh: 閏月，壬戌朔，師古薨。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the new moon of the day renxu, Shigu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the first day of renxu, Li Shigu died.

sentences.zh: 沐、公度秘不發喪，潛逆師道於密州，奉以爲節度副使。

translations.literal: Mu and Gongdu kept the death secret and did not announce the mourning; secretly they went to meet Shidao at Mizhou and installed him as vice military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu and Li Gongdu concealed the death, sent secretly for Shidao at Mizhou, and installed him as vice military governor.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，癸丑，髙崇文破劉闢之衆萬人於玄武。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the day guichou, Gao Chongwen defeated ten thousand of Liu Pi's forces at Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the guichou day, Gao Chongwen routed ten thousand of Liu Pi's troops at Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 甲午，詔：「凡西川繼援之兵，悉取崇文處分。」

translations.literal: On the day jiawu, an edict: "All reinforcements sent to aid Western Shu shall entirely be disposed of by Chongwen."
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day an edict declared: "All troops sent as reinforcements to Western Shu shall be placed entirely under Gao Chongwen's command."

sentences.zh: 壬寅，葬至德大聖大安孝皇帝於豐陵，廟號順宗。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, the late Emperor of the posthumous title Zhide Dasheng Da'an Xiaohuangdi was buried at Fengling; his temple name is Shunzong.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Emperor Shunzong—posthumously titled Zhide Dasheng Da'an Xiaohuangdi—was buried at Fengling.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬戌，以妃郭氏爲貴妃。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on the day renxu, Consort Guo was made Honored Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the renxu day, Lady Guo was elevated to Honored Consort.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，立皇子寧爲鄧王，寬爲澧王，宥爲遂王，察爲深王，寰爲洋王，寮爲絳王，審爲建王。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, the princes were enfeoffed: Ning as Prince of Deng, Kuan as Prince of Li, You as Prince of Sui, Cha as Prince of Shen, Huan as Prince of Yang, Liao as Prince of Jiang, and Shen as Prince of Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day the Emperor enfeoffed his sons: Ning as Prince of Deng, Kuan as Prince of Li, You as Prince of Sui, Cha as Prince of Shen, Huan as Prince of Yang, Liao as Prince of Jiang, and Shen as Prince of Jian.

sentences.zh: 李師道總軍務，久之，朝命未至。

translations.literal: Li Shidao took charge of military affairs; after a long time, the court appointment had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao assumed control of military affairs, but for a long while no appointment arrived from court.

sentences.zh: 師道謀於將佐，或請出兵掠四境。

translations.literal: Shidao consulted with his officers and staff; some urged sending troops to raid the borders on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao consulted his officers and staff; some urged raiding the neighboring territories with troops.

sentences.zh: 髙沐固止之，請輸兩稅，申官吏，行鹽法，遣使相繼奉表詣京師。

translations.literal: Gao Mu firmly restrained him, urging him to submit the two tax levies, appoint officials properly, enforce the salt monopoly law, and send envoys in succession with memorials to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Mu firmly dissuaded him, urging instead that he remit the land and labor taxes, confirm official appointments, enforce the salt monopoly, and send a stream of envoys with memorials to the capital.

sentences.zh: 杜黃裳請乘其未定而分之。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang urged taking advantage while Shidao was not yet settled to divide the command.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang urged the court to move while Shidao was still unsettled and partition the command.

sentences.zh: 上以劉闢未平，己巳，以師道爲平盧留後、知鄆州事。

translations.literal: Because Liu Pi had not yet been pacified, on the day jisi the Emperor appointed Shidao as acting military governor of Pinglu and administrator of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With Liu Pi still undefeated, the Emperor on the jisi day appointed Shidao acting military governor of Pinglu and administrator of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 堂後主書滑渙久在中書，與知樞密劉光琦相結，宰相議事有與光琦異者，令渙達意，常得所欲，杜佑、鄭絪等皆低意善視之。

translations.literal: Hua Huan, chief clerk behind the hall, had long been in the Secretariat and colluded with Liu Guangqi, who handled confidential affairs; when the chief ministers deliberated and disagreed with Guangqi, they had Huan convey their intent, and usually got what they wanted. Du You, Zheng Yin, and others all lowered their will and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Huan, a chief clerk of the Secretariat, had long served there and was allied with Liu Guangqi of the Bureau of Military Affairs. When the chief ministers deliberated against Guangqi's wishes, Huan would carry their views to him, and they usually got their way. Du You, Zheng Yin, and others all deferred to him graciously.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶與諸相議事，渙從旁指陳是非，餘慶怒叱之。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yuqing and the other chief ministers deliberated affairs, Huan from the side pointed out right and wrong; Yuqing angrily shouted him down.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing and the other chief ministers were deliberating, Huan interjected from the side to judge right and wrong; Yuqing angrily rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，罷相。

translations.literal: Before long, he was removed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Zheng Yuqing was dismissed from the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 四方賂遺無虚日，中書舍人李吉甫言其專恣，請去之。

translations.literal: Gifts and bribes from all quarters came without a single day empty; Secretariat drafter Li Jifu spoke of his arbitrary power and requested his removal.
translations.idiomatic: Bribes from every quarter arrived daily without fail. Li Jifu, a Secretariat drafter, denounced Huan's arbitrary conduct and asked that he be removed.

sentences.zh: 上命宰相闔中書四門搜掩，盡得其奸狀，九月。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the chief ministers to close and search all four gates of the Secretariat, completely obtaining evidence of his wicked conduct—in the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered the chief ministers to seal the four gates of the Secretariat and search it, uncovering the full extent of his corruption—in the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，貶渙雷州司戸，尋賜死。

translations.literal: On the day xinchou, Huan was demoted to clerk of Leizhou; soon he was ordered to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day, Hua Huan was demoted to registrar of Leizhou and soon afterward was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 籍沒，家財凡數千萬。

translations.literal: His property was confiscated; household wealth totaled tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: His property was confiscated; his household goods were worth tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，髙崇文又敗劉闢之衆於鹿頭關，嚴秦敗劉闢之衆於神泉。

translations.literal: On the day renyin, Gao Chongwen again defeated Liu Pi's forces at Lutou Pass, and Yan Qin defeated Liu Pi's forces at Shenquan.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin day, Gao Chongwen again routed Liu Pi's army at Lutou Pass, while Yan Qin defeated another body of Pi's troops at Shenquan.

sentences.zh: 河東將阿跌光顏將兵會髙崇文於行營，愆期一日，懼誅，欲深入自贖，軍於鹿頭之西，斷其糧道，城中憂懼。

translations.literal: The Hedong general Adie Guangyan led troops to join Gao Chongwen at the campaign headquarters; he was one day late and feared execution; wishing to redeem himself by advancing deeply, he encamped west of Lutou and cut off their supply routes—the city was filled with worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Adie Guangyan, a Hedong general, brought his troops to Gao Chongwen's field headquarters. Having arrived one day late, he feared punishment and sought to redeem himself with a bold stroke: he camped west of Lutou and severed the rebels' supply lines, throwing the garrison into alarm.

sentences.zh: 於是闢、綿江柵將李文悅、鹿頭守將仇良輔皆以城降於崇文。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commanders of Pi's fortifications at Mianjiang, Li Wenyu, and of Lutou, Qiu Liangfu, both surrendered their cities to Chongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Wenyu, commander of Pi's stockade at Mianjiang, and Qiu Liangfu, defender of Lutou, both surrendered their posts to Gao Chongwen.

sentences.zh: 獲闢婿蘇強，士卒降者萬計。

translations.literal: Pi's son-in-law Su Qiang was captured; soldiers who surrendered numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pi's son-in-law Su Qiang was taken prisoner, and rebel soldiers surrendered by the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 崇文遂長驅直指成都，所向崩潰，軍不留行。

translations.literal: Chongwen then drove straight for Chengdu; wherever he went, the enemy collapsed; the army did not halt its advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen then pressed straight toward Chengdu; wherever he turned, the enemy crumbled, and his army did not slacken its march.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，克成都。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, Chengdu was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, Chengdu fell.

sentences.zh: 劉闢、盧文若帥數十騎西奔吐蕃，崇文使髙霞寓等追之，及於羊灌田。

translations.literal: Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo led several dozen horsemen fleeing west toward Tibet; Chongwen sent Gao Xiayu and others to pursue them, catching up at Yangguantian.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi and Lu Wenruo fled west toward Tibet with several dozen horsemen; Chongwen sent Gao Xiayu and others in pursuit and overtook them at Yangguantian.

sentences.zh: 闢赴江不死，擒之。

translations.literal: Pi threw himself into the river but did not die and was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi threw himself into the river but failed to drown and was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 文若先殺妻子，乃系石自沉。

translations.literal: Wenruo first killed his wife and children, then tied stones to himself and sank.
translations.idiomatic: Wenruo first killed his wife and children, then weighted himself with stones and drowned.

sentences.zh: 崇文入成都，屯於通衢，休息士卒，市肆不驚，珍寶山積，秋毫不犯，檻劉闢送京師。

translations.literal: Chongwen entered Chengdu, encamped at the main thoroughfare, rested the troops—the markets were undisturbed; treasures piled mountain-high, yet not a hair was violated; Liu Pi was caged and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen entered Chengdu and encamped in the main thoroughfare to rest his troops; the markets were undisturbed, treasures lay heaped like hills, yet not a thing was plundered. Liu Pi was placed in a cage and sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 斬闢大將邢泚、館驛巡官沈衍，餘無所問。

translations.literal: He executed Pi's senior generals Xing Ci and the post-station inspector Shen Yan; of the rest, none were questioned.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Liu Pi's senior general Xing Ci and the post-station inspector Shen Yan; beyond that, no one else was prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 軍府事無鉅細，命一遵韋南康故事，從容指手爲，一境皆平。

translations.literal: Military and administrative affairs great and small—all orders followed the precedent of Wei Gao of Nankang; proceeding with composure, he directed affairs with a wave of the hand, and the whole region was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Great and small matters of the military government alike were ordered according to the precedent set by Wei Gao of Nankang; with unruffled ease he directed affairs at a gesture, and the whole circuit was settled.

sentences.zh: 初，韋皋以西山運糧使崔從知邛州事，劉闢反，從以書諫闢；

translations.literal: Initially, when Wei Gao had Cui Cong, grain transport commissioner for the Western Mountains, administer Qiong Prefecture, and when Liu Pi rebelled, Cong wrote to remonstrate with Pi;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Wei Gao had put Cui Cong, commissioner for grain transport in the Western Mountains, in charge of Qiong Prefecture. When Liu Pi rebelled, Cong wrote to remonstrate with him;

sentences.zh: 闢發兵攻之，從嬰城固守；

translations.literal: Pi raised troops to attack him; Cong closed the city and held firm;
translations.idiomatic: Pi sent troops against him; Cong shut the city gates and held out;

sentences.zh: 闢敗，乃得免。

translations.literal: when Pi was defeated, he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: when Pi was defeated, Cong was spared.

sentences.zh: 從，融之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Cong was the great-grandson of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cong was the great-grandson of Cui Rong.

sentences.zh: 韋皋參佐房式、韋乾度、獨孤密、符載、郗士美、段文昌等素服麻屨，銜土請罪。

translations.literal: Wei Gao's staff members Fang Shi, Wei Qiandu, Dugu Mi, Fu Zai, Xi Shimei, Duan Wenchang, and others wore white hemp and straw sandals, held earth in their mouths, and asked to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gao's staff—Fang Shi, Wei Qiandu, Dugu Mi, Fu Zai, Xi Shimei, Duan Wenchang, and others—came in white hemp and straw sandals with earth in their mouths to submit themselves for punishment.

sentences.zh: 崇文皆釋而禮之，草表薦式等，厚贐而遣之。

translations.literal: Chongwen released them all and treated them with courtesy; he drafted a memorial recommending Shi and the others, gave them generous parting gifts, and sent them off.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen released them all and received them with courtesy, drafted a memorial recommending Fang Shi and the rest, gave them rich parting gifts, and sent them on their way.

sentences.zh: 目段文昌曰：「君必爲將相，未敢奉薦。」

translations.literal: He looked at Duan Wenchang and said: "You are certain to become a general or chief minister—I dare not recommend you."
translations.idiomatic: He looked at Duan Wenchang and said, "You are destined for high office as general or chief minister—I dare not presume to recommend you.

sentences.zh: 載，廬山人；

translations.literal: Zai was a man of Lushan;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zai was a native of Lushan;

sentences.zh: 式，琯之從子；

translations.literal: Shi was the nephew of Guan;
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shi was a nephew of Fang Guan;

sentences.zh: 文昌，志玄之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Wenchang was the great-great-grandson of Zhixuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchang was the great-great-grandson of Duan Zhixuan.

sentences.zh: 闢有二妾，皆殊色，監軍請獻之，崇曰：「天子命我討平凶豎，當以撫百姓爲先，遽獻婦人以求媚，豈天子之意邪！

translations.literal: Pi had two concubines, both of exceptional beauty; the army supervisor requested they be presented as tribute. Chongwen said: "Heaven's son ordered me to suppress and pacify the wicked rebel—I should put comforting the people first; to hastily present women seeking favor—is that Heaven's son's intent?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pi had two concubines of striking beauty, and the army supervisor asked that they be sent up as tribute. Gao Chongwen said, "The Son of Heaven sent me to crush a wicked rebel; my first duty is to reassure the people. To hurry women forward as a gift of flattery—would that be the Son of Heaven's intent?

sentences.zh: 崇文義不爲此。」

translations.literal: Chongwen, on principle, would not do this."
translations.idiomatic: On principle, Gao Chongwen would not do it."

sentences.zh: 乃以配將吏之無妻者。

translations.literal: He then matched them to officers and clerks who had no wives.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he gave them in marriage to officers and clerks who had no wives.

sentences.zh: 杜黃裳建議征蜀及指受髙崇文方略，皆懸合事宜。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang's proposals to campaign against Shu and to instruct and accept Gao Chongwen's strategy all accorded perfectly with circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang's counsel to campaign against Shu and his instructions to Gao Chongwen on strategy all proved perfectly suited to the situation.

sentences.zh: 崇文素憚劉澭，黃裳使謂之曰：「若無功，當以劉澭相代。」

translations.literal: Chongwen had long feared Liu Yong; Huangshang had someone tell him: "If you achieve no merit, Liu Yong will replace you."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chongwen had long stood in awe of Liu Yong; Huangshang sent word to him: "If you fail to win distinction, Liu Yong will take your place.

sentences.zh: 故能得其死力。

translations.literal: Thus he was able to obtain Chongwen's utmost exertion.
translations.idiomatic: That was how he secured Gao Chongwen's utmost effort.

sentences.zh: 及蜀平，宰相入賀，上目黃裳曰：「卿之功也！」

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, the chief ministers entered to congratulate; the Emperor looked at Huangshang and said: "This is your achievement!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shu was pacified, the chief ministers came to offer congratulations; the Emperor turned to Du Huangshang and said, "This victory is yours!"

sentences.zh: 辛巳，詔征少室山人李渤爲左拾遺。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, an edict summoned Li Bo the recluse of Shaoshi Mountain as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day an edict summoned Li Bo, the recluse of Shaoshi Mountain, to serve as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 渤辭疾不至，然朝政有得失，渤輒附奏陳論。

translations.literal: Bo declined on grounds of illness and did not come; yet whenever the court's governance had merit or fault, Bo would attach memorials setting forth arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Li Bo pleaded illness and did not come to court, yet whenever he saw merit or fault in the administration he would submit memorials setting out his views.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲子，易定節度使張茂昭入朝。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on the day jiazi, Zhang Maozhao, military governor of Yiding, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the jiazi day, Zhang Maozhao, military governor of Yiding, arrived at court.

sentences.zh: 制割資、簡、陵、榮、昌、瀘六州隸東川。

translations.literal: An edict carved away Zi, Jian, Ling, Rong, Chang, and Lu six prefectures and subordinated them to Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict detached the six prefectures of Zi, Jian, Ling, Rong, Chang, and Lu and placed them under Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 房式等未至京師，皆除省寺官。

translations.literal: Before Fang Shi and the others reached the capital, they were all appointed to posts in the central ministries and directorates.
translations.idiomatic: Before Fang Shi and the others even reached the capital, they were all given posts in the central ministries and directorates.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以髙崇文爲西川節度使。

translations.literal: On the day bingyin, Gao Chongwen was made military governor of Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Gao Chongwen was appointed military governor of Western Shu.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，以嚴礪爲東川節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, Yan Li was made military governor of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuchen day, Yan Li was made military governor of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以將作監柳晟爲山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu, Liu Sheng, Director of Imperial Construction, was made military governor of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day, Liu Sheng, Director of Imperial Construction, was appointed military governor of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 晟至漢中，府兵討劉闢還，未至城，詔復遣戍梓州，軍士怨怒，，脅監軍，謀作亂。

translations.literal: When Sheng reached Hanzhong, the prefectural troops returning from campaigning against Liu Pi had not yet reached the city when an edict again ordered them sent to garrison Zizhou; the soldiers were resentful and angry, coerced the army supervisor, and plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Sheng reached Hanzhong, the prefectural troops returning from the campaign against Liu Pi had not yet entered the city when an edict arrived ordering them back to garrison Zizhou. The men grew resentful, intimidated the army supervisor, and plotted mutiny.

sentences.zh: 晟聞之，疾驅入城，慰勞之，既而問曰：「汝曹何以得成功？」

translations.literal: When Sheng heard of it, he galloped into the city, comforted and rewarded them; then he asked: "How did you gentlemen achieve success?"
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Sheng heard of it, he galloped into the city and went among the men to comfort them; then he asked, "How was it that you won your victory?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「誅反者劉闢耳。」

translations.literal: They answered: "By executing the rebel Liu Pi."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "By putting down the rebel Liu Pi—that is all."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「辟以不受詔命，故汝曹得以立功，豈可復使它人誅汝以爲功邪？」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "Pi, because he did not accept the imperial command, enabled you gentlemen to achieve merit—how can you again let others execute you to achieve merit?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng said, "Liu Pi refused the imperial command, and that is why you were able to win merit. Would you now let someone else kill you to win merit of his own?"

sentences.zh: 衆皆拜謝，請詣戍所如詔書。

translations.literal: The crowd all bowed in thanks and requested to go to the garrison post as the edict commanded.
translations.idiomatic: The men all bowed in acknowledgment and asked to proceed to their garrison as the edict directed.

sentences.zh: 軍府由是獲安。

translations.literal: The military headquarters was thereby secured in peace.
translations.idiomatic: The headquarters was thereby restored to order.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以平盧留後李師道爲節度使。

translations.literal: On the day renwu, Li Shidao, acting military governor of Pinglu, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day, Li Shidao, acting military governor of Pinglu, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 戊子，劉闢至長安，並族黨誅之。

translations.literal: On the day wuzi, Liu Pi reached Chang'an; he and his clan associates were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuzi day, Liu Pi arrived at Chang'an and was executed together with his kinsmen and followers.

sentences.zh: 武寧節度使張愔有疾，上表請代。

translations.literal: Zhang Yin, military governor of Wuning, was ill and submitted a memorial requesting replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yin, military governor of Wuning, fell ill and memorialized the throne asking to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊申，征愔爲工部尚書，以東都留守王紹代之，復以濠、泗二州隸武寧軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the day wushen, Yin was summoned as Minister of Works; Wang Shao, Eastern Capital garrison commander, replaced him; Hao and Si two prefectures were again subordinated to the Wuning army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the wushen day, Zhang Yin was recalled as Minister of Works and replaced by Wang Shao, garrison commander of the Eastern Capital; the prefectures of Hao and Si were again placed under the Wuning command.

sentences.zh: 徐人喜得二州，故不爲亂。

translations.literal: The people of Xu Prefecture were pleased to regain the two prefectures, and therefore did not stir up trouble.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Xu were glad to recover the two prefectures, and so no unrest broke out.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以内常侍吐突承璀爲左神策中尉。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, the inner palace attendant Tuhu Chenghui was made Central Commander of the Left Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day, the inner attendant Tuhu Chenghui was appointed Central Commander of the Left Shence Army.

sentences.zh: 承璀事上於東宮，以干敏得幸。

translations.literal: Chenghui had served the Emperor in the Eastern Palace and won favor through cleverness and quickness.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui had served the Emperor when he was heir in the Eastern Palace and won favor through his quick wit.

sentences.zh: 是歳，回鶻入貢，始以摩尼偕來，於中國置寺處之。

translations.literal: That year, the Uyghurs came bearing tribute; for the first time Manichaean priests came along with them, and temples were established in China to house them.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Uyghurs sent tribute, and for the first time Manichaean priests came with them; temples were established in China to receive them.

sentences.zh: 其法日晏乃食，食葷而不食湩酪。

translations.literal: Their law: they eat only after sundown; they eat meat but do not eat dairy.
translations.idiomatic: Their practice was to eat only after sunset; they ate meat but abstained from milk and curds.

sentences.zh: 回鶻信奉之，可汗或與議國事。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs believed in it; the kaghan sometimes deliberated state affairs with them.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs embraced the faith, and the kaghan sometimes consulted Manichaean priests on affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛卯，上祀圓丘，赦天下。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day xinmao, the Emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound and amnestied all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the xinmao day, the Emperor sacrificed at the Circular Mound and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上以杜佑髙年重德，禮重之，常呼司徒而不名。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Du You was of advanced age and great virtue, showed him heavy respect, often addressing him as Minister of Works without using his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Because Du You was advanced in years and held in high esteem, the Emperor treated him with exceptional respect, often addressing him as Minister of Works rather than by name.

sentences.zh: 佑以老疾，請致仕。

translations.literal: You, due to old age and illness, requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Du You, citing age and illness, asked to retire from office.

sentences.zh: 詔令佑毎月入朝不過再三，因至中書議大政。

translations.literal: An edict ordered You to attend court no more than two or three times a month, and when he came, to proceed to the Secretariat to discuss major policy.
translations.idiomatic: An edict allowed Du You to attend court no more than two or three times a month, and on those occasions to come to the Secretariat to discuss major affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 它日聽歸樊川。

translations.literal: On other days he was permitted to return to Fanchuan.
translations.idiomatic: On other days he was free to return to his estate at Fanchuan.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郎、同平章事杜黃裳，有經濟大略而不修小節，故不得久在相位。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Chancellor Du Huangchang possessed broad economic vision but did not attend to minor proprieties, and therefore could not long remain in the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Chancellor, had a grand grasp of statecraft but little patience for small decorum, and so could not keep his seat at the helm for long.

sentences.zh: 乙巳以黃裳同平章事，充河中、晉、絳、慈、隰節度使。

translations.literal: On yisi day Huangchang was made Co-Chancellor and appointed military governor of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day Du Huangchang was named Co-Chancellor and sent out as military governor of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 己酉，以戸部侍郎武元衡爲門下侍郎，翰林學士李吉甫爲中書侍郎，並同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiyou day, Minister of Revenue Wu Yuanheng was made Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Hanlin Academician Li Jifu was made Vice Minister of the Secretariat; both were appointed Co-Chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day Wu Yuanheng, Minister of Revenue, became Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and Li Jifu, Hanlin Academician, became Vice Minister of the Secretariat; both were named Co-Chancellors.

sentences.zh: 吉甫聞之感泣，謂中書舍人裴垍曰：「吉甫流落江、淮，逾十五年，一旦蒙恩至此。

translations.literal: When Jifu heard this he wept with emotion and said to Secretariat Drafter Pei Ji: "Jifu wandered in exile along the Yangzi and Huai rivers for more than fifteen years, and in a single moment I have received grace to reach this place.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu heard the news he wept with gratitude and said to Pei Ji, drafter of the Secretariat: "I wandered in exile along the Yangzi and Huai for more than fifteen years, and now, in a single stroke of grace, I have risen to this.

sentences.zh: 思所以報德，惟在進賢，而朝廷後進，罕所接識，君有精鑒，願悉爲我言之。」

translations.literal: Thinking how to repay this kindness, I can only do so by promoting worthy men. Yet among the newer men at court I have scarcely made acquaintance. You have keen judgment; I beg you to tell me of them all."
translations.idiomatic: The only way I can repay this debt is to advance worthy men. But among the rising officials at court I know almost no one. You have a sharp eye for talent; please tell me of everyone you would recommend."

sentences.zh: 垍取筆疎三十餘人，數月之間，選用略盡。

translations.literal: Ji took up his brush and listed more than thirty men; within a few months Jifu had appointed nearly all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji took up his brush and wrote out more than thirty names, and within a few months Li Jifu had appointed nearly all of them.

sentences.zh: 當時翕然稱吉甫爲得人。

translations.literal: At the time people unanimously praised Jifu for having found the right men.
translations.idiomatic: At the time everyone agreed that Li Jifu had a gift for finding the right men.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸酉，邕州奏破黃賊，獲其酋長黃承慶。

translations.literal: In the second month, on guiyou day, Yong Prefecture reported defeating the Yellow Bandits and capturing their chieftain Huang Chengqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on guiyou day, Yong Prefecture reported that it had broken the Yellow Bandits and captured their chieftain Huang Chengqing.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，甲子，以右金吾大將軍范希朝爲朔方、靈、鹽節度使，以右神策、鹽州、定遠兵隸焉，以革舊弊，任邊將也。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi day, Right Commander of the Golden Grips Fan Xichao was made military governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan; the Right Shence Army and the Yanzhou and Dingyuan garrisons were placed under his command, to reform old abuses and entrust border affairs to a frontier general.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on jiazi day, Fan Xichao, Right Commander of the Golden Grips, was made military governor of Shuofang, Ling, and Yan, with the Right Shence Army and the Yanzhou and Dingyuan garrisons placed under him—a move meant to cure old abuses by putting the frontier in the hands of a border general.

sentences.zh: 秋、八月，劉濟、王士眞、張茂昭爭私隙，迭相表請加罪。

translations.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, Liu Ji, Wang Shizhen, and Zhang Maozhao nursed private grievances against one another and repeatedly sent memorials asking that the others be punished.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the eighth month, Liu Ji, Wang Shizhen, and Zhang Maozhao were at odds over private slights and kept sending memorials asking the throne to punish one another.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，以給事中房式爲幽州、成德、義武宣慰使，和解之。

translations.literal: On wuyin day, Supervising Secretary Fang Shi was made pacification commissioner for Youzhou, Chengde, and Yiwu to mediate and reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Fang Shi, Supervising Secretary, was sent as pacification commissioner to Youzhou, Chengde, and Yiwu to settle their dispute.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙酉，密王綢薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yiyou day, Prince Mi Wang Chou died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yiyou day, Prince Mi, Wang Chou, died.

sentences.zh: 夏、蜀既平，籓鎭惕息，多求入朝。

translations.literal: After the Summer Rebellion and Shu were pacified, the frontier garrisons grew watchful and subdued, and many sought permission to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Summer Rebellion and Shu had been pacified, the regional garrisons grew cautious and quiet, and many asked to come to court.

sentences.zh: 鎭海節度使李錡亦不自安，求入朝，上許之。

translations.literal: Li Qi, military governor of Zhenhai, also felt ill at ease, requested to come to court, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, military governor of Zhenhai, was likewise uneasy and asked to come to court; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遣中使至京口慰撫，且勞其將士。

translations.literal: The court sent an imperial envoy to Jingkou to console and reassure him, and also to reward his officers and men.
translations.idiomatic: The throne sent an imperial envoy to Jingkou to reassure him and to reward his officers and troops.

sentences.zh: 錡雖署判官王澹爲留後，實無行意，屢遷行期，澹與敕使數勸諭之。

translations.literal: Although Qi appointed his aide Wang Dan as acting governor, he truly had no intention of going and repeatedly postponed his departure. Wang Dan and the imperial envoy often urged and admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi did appoint his aide Wang Dan acting governor, but he had no real intention of leaving and kept putting off his departure. Wang Dan and the imperial envoy repeatedly urged him to go.

sentences.zh: 錡不悅，上表稱疾，請至歳暮入朝。

translations.literal: Qi was displeased and submitted a memorial claiming illness, asking to come to court only at year's end.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, Qi submitted a memorial claiming illness and asking to delay his arrival until the year's end.

sentences.zh: 上以問宰相，武元衡曰：「陛下初即政，錡求朝得朝，求止得止，可否在錡，將何以令四海！」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chancellors. Wu Yuanheng said: "Your Majesty has only just ascended the throne. If Qi asks to come to court and is allowed to come, and asks to stay and is allowed to stay—if approval or denial rests with Qi, how will Your Majesty command the realm!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the chancellors. Wu Yuanheng said: "Your Majesty has only just taken the throne. If Li Qi asks to come to court and may come, and asks to stay and may stay—if yes or no rests with Li Qi, how will you command the realm!

sentences.zh: 上以爲然，下詔征之。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this right and issued an edict summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and issued an edict summoning him to court.

sentences.zh: 錡詐窮，遂謀反。

translations.literal: Qi, his stratagems exhausted, then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: With his deceptions exhausted, Li Qi then plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 王澹既掌留務，於軍府頗有制置，錡益不平，密諭親兵使殺之。

translations.literal: Once Wang Dan took charge of affairs as acting governor, he made quite a few arrangements within the headquarters. Qi grew all the more resentful and secretly instructed his personal troops to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Once Wang Dan was running affairs as acting governor, he began making his own arrangements in headquarters. Li Qi grew still angrier and secretly told his personal guard to kill him.

sentences.zh: 會頒冬服，錡嚴兵坐幄中，澹與敕使入謁，有軍士數百噪於庭曰：「王澹何人，擅主軍務！」

translations.literal: It happened that winter uniforms were being issued. Qi sat in his pavilion with troops drawn up in tight order. Wang Dan and the imperial envoy entered to pay their respects. Several hundred soldiers clamored in the courtyard, saying: "Who is Wang Dan, that he dares on his own authority to direct military affairs!
translations.idiomatic: Winter uniforms were being issued. Li Qi sat in his pavilion surrounded by armed men while Wang Dan and the imperial envoy came to pay their respects. Several hundred soldiers shouted in the courtyard: "Who is Wang Dan to take command of military affairs on his own!

sentences.zh: 曳下，臠食之；

translations.literal: They dragged him down and tore his flesh to pieces and ate it;
translations.idiomatic: They dragged him down, hacked his flesh to pieces, and ate it;

sentences.zh: 大將趙琦出慰止，又臠食之；

translations.literal: General Zhao Qi came out to calm and restrain them, and they tore his flesh to pieces and ate him as well;
translations.idiomatic: General Zhao Qi came out to calm them, and they hacked him to pieces and ate him too;

sentences.zh: 注刃於敕使之頸，詬詈，將殺之。

translations.literal: They put blades to the imperial envoy's neck, cursed and reviled him, and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: They pressed blades to the imperial envoy's neck, cursed him, and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 錡陽驚，起救之。

translations.literal: Qi feigned alarm and rose to rescue him.
