translations.idiomatic: Li Qi pretended to be shocked and rose to save him.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，己未，詔征錡爲左僕射，以御史大夫李元素爲鎭海節度使。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei day, an edict summoned Qi to the post of Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; Supervising Censor Li Yuansu was made military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiwei day, an edict summoned Li Qi to the capital as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat and appointed Li Yuansu, Supervising Censor, military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 庚申，錡表言軍變，殺留後、大將。

translations.literal: On gengshen day, Qi submitted a memorial saying that there had been a military mutiny that killed the acting governor and a general.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day Li Qi submitted a memorial claiming a mutiny had killed the acting governor and a general.

sentences.zh: 先是，錡選腹心五人爲所部五州鎭將，姚志安處蘇州，李深處常州，趙惟忠處湖州，丘自昌處杭州，髙肅處睦州，各有兵數千，伺察刺史動靜。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qi had chosen five trusted men as garrison commanders over the five prefectures under his jurisdiction: Yao Zhi'an at Suzhou, Li Shen at Changzhou, Zhao Weizhong at Huzhou, Qiu Zichang at Hangzhou, and Gao Su at Muzhou. Each had several thousand troops and kept watch on the movements of the prefectural governors.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Qi had placed five trusted men as garrison commanders over his five prefectures: Yao Zhi'an at Suzhou, Li Shen at Changzhou, Zhao Weizhong at Huzhou, Qiu Zichang at Hangzhou, and Gao Su at Muzhou. Each commanded several thousand men and watched the prefects' every move.

sentences.zh: 至是，錡各使殺其刺史，遣牙將庚伯良將兵三千治石頭城。

translations.literal: At this point Qi had each of them kill his prefectural governor and sent staff officer Geng Boliang to lead three thousand troops to fortify Shitou Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Li Qi had each of them kill his prefect and sent staff officer Geng Boliang with three thousand troops to fortify Shitou Fortress.

sentences.zh: 常州刺史顏防用客李雲計，矯制稱招討副使，斬李深，傳檄蘇、杭、湖、睦。

translations.literal: Changzhou Prefect Yan Fang, using a plan offered by his guest Li Yun, forged an order naming himself deputy campaign commander, executed Li Shen, and issued proclamations to Suzhou, Hangzhou, Huzhou, and Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Fang, prefect of Changzhou, took a plan from his retainer Li Yun, forged an order naming himself deputy campaign commander, executed Li Shen, and sent proclamations to Suzhou, Hangzhou, Huzhou, and Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 請同進討。

translations.literal: He asked them to join in a common advance to suppress the rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He called on them to advance together against the rebel.

sentences.zh: 湖州刺史辛秘潛募鄕閭子弟數百，夜襲趙惟忠營，斬之。

translations.literal: Huzhou Prefect Xin Mi secretly recruited several hundred men from the local communities and, by night, raided Zhao Weizhong's camp and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Xin Mi, prefect of Huzhou, secretly raised several hundred local youths, raided Zhao Weizhong's camp by night, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 蘇州刺史李素爲姚志安所敗，生致於錡，具桎梏釘於船舷，未及京口，會錡敗，得免。

translations.literal: Suzhou Prefect Li Su was defeated by Yao Zhi'an, taken alive to Qi, fitted with fetters and nailed to the side of a boat. Before reaching Jingkou, Qi was defeated and Li Su was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Su, prefect of Suzhou, was defeated by Yao Zhi'an, taken alive to Li Qi, shackled and nailed to a boat's side. Before they reached Jingkou, Li Qi fell, and Li Su was spared.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，制削李錡官爵及屬籍。

translations.literal: On yichou day, an edict stripped Li Qi of his offices, ranks, and registration in the imperial clan rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day an edict stripped Li Qi of his offices, titles, and place in the imperial clan register.

sentences.zh: 以淮南節度使王鍔統諸道兵爲招討處置使，征宣武、義寧、武昌兵並淮南、宣歙兵倶出宣州，江西兵出信州，浙東兵出杭州，以討之。

translations.literal: Wang E, military governor of Huainan, was put in overall command of armies from all circuits as campaign and disposition commissioner. Armies from Xuanwu, Yining, and Wuchang, together with troops from Huainan and Xuanshe, were all to advance from Xuanzhou; Jiangxi troops from Xinzhou; Zhedong troops from Hangzhou—to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, military governor of Huainan, was made overall campaign commander. Troops from Xuanwu, Yining, and Wuchang, together with forces from Huainan and Xuanshe, were to move out from Xuanzhou; Jiangxi troops from Xinzhou; Zhedong troops from Hangzhou—all to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 髙崇文在蜀期年，一旦謂監軍曰：「崇文，河朔一卒，幸有功。

translations.literal: After a full year in Shu, Gao Chongwen one day said to the army supervisor: "Chongwen is but a soldier from north of the Yellow River who, by good fortune, achieved some merit.
translations.idiomatic: After a year in Shu, Gao Chongwen one day told the army supervisor: "I am only a soldier from Hebei who, by luck, won some merit.

sentences.zh: 致位至此。

translations.literal: I have risen to this rank.
translations.idiomatic: I have risen to this rank.

sentences.zh: 西川乃宰相迴翔之地，崇文叨居日久，豈敢自安！」

translations.literal: The Western Circuit is where chancellors wheel and soar; Chongwen has presumptuously occupied this post too long—how could I dare feel secure!"
translations.idiomatic: The Western Circuit is where chancellors come and go; I have presumptuously held this post too long—how could I feel at ease!"

sentences.zh: 屢上表稱「蜀中安逸，無所陳力，願效死邊陲。」

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials saying: "Shu is peaceful and secure; there is nowhere I can exert my strength. I wish to offer my life on the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized the throne: "Shu is peaceful; I have no work worthy of me here. I wish to serve unto death on the frontier."

sentences.zh: 上擇可以代崇文者而難其人。

translations.literal: The emperor sought someone who could replace Chongwen but found it hard to choose the right man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked for someone to replace Chongwen but found no obvious choice.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，以門下侍郎、同平章事武元衡同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: On dingmao day, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Chancellor Wu Yuanheng was retained as Co-Chancellor and appointed military governor of the Western Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day Wu Yuanheng, Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Co-Chancellor, kept his chancellorship and was appointed military governor of the Western Circuit.

sentences.zh: 李錡以宣州富饒，欲先取之，遣兵馬使張子良、李奉仙、田少卿將兵三千襲之。

translations.literal: Li Qi, regarding Xuanzhou as rich and fertile, wished to seize it first. He sent Military Commissioner Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing to lead three thousand troops in a surprise attack on it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi, seeing Xuanzhou as rich territory, wanted to take it first and sent Military Commissioners Zhang Ziliang, Li Fengxian, and Tian Shaoqing with three thousand men to strike it.

sentences.zh: 三人知錡必敗，與牙將裴行立同謀討之。

translations.literal: The three men knew Qi was bound to be defeated. Together with staff officer Pei Xingli they plotted to turn against him and suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: The three men knew Li Qi was doomed. With staff officer Pei Xingli they plotted to turn on him and bring him down.

sentences.zh: 行立，錡之甥也，故悉知錡之密謀。

translations.literal: Xingli was Qi's nephew and therefore knew all of Qi's secret plans.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingli was Li Qi's nephew and therefore knew all his secret plans.

sentences.zh: 三將營於城外，將發，召士卒諭之曰：「僕射反逆，官軍四集，常、湖二將繼死，其勢已蹙。

translations.literal: The three generals encamped outside the city. As they were about to set out, they assembled the troops and addressed them: "The Vice Director has rebelled. Government armies are gathering from all sides. The commanders at Chang and Hu have already been killed in succession. His position is already tight.
translations.idiomatic: The three generals camped outside the city. As they were about to march, they gathered the troops and said: "The Vice Director has rebelled. Imperial armies are closing in from every side. The commanders at Chang and Hu are already dead. His cause is already desperate.

sentences.zh: 今乃欲使吾輩遠取宣城，吾輩何爲隨之族滅！

translations.literal: And now he would have us go far away to seize Xuancheng—why should we follow him to extermination of our clans!
translations.idiomatic: And now he wants us to march far off to take Xuancheng—why should we follow him to the destruction of our families!

sentences.zh: 豈若去逆效順，轉禍爲福乎！」

translations.literal: Would it not be better to abandon the rebel and show loyalty, turning calamity into blessing!"
translations.idiomatic: Would it not be better to cast off the rebel, show loyalty, and turn disaster into blessing!"

sentences.zh: 衆悅，許諾，即夜，還趨城。

translations.literal: The troops were pleased and pledged themselves. That same night they turned back and marched on the city.
translations.idiomatic: The men were won over and pledged themselves. That same night they turned back and rushed the city.

sentences.zh: 行立舉火鼓噪，應之於内，引兵趨牙門。

translations.literal: Xingli raised signal fires and raised a clamor. Those inside responded, and he led troops toward the headquarters gate.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingli lit signal fires and raised a clamor. Men inside answered, and he led troops toward headquarters.

sentences.zh: 錡聞子良等舉兵，怒，聞行立應之，撫膺曰：「吾何望矣！」

translations.literal: When Qi heard that Ziliang and the others had risen in arms he was furious. When he heard that Xingli had answered from within, he beat his breast and said: "What hope have I left!
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi heard that Ziliang and the others had risen in arms he was furious. When he heard Pei Xingli answering from within, he beat his breast and cried: "What hope is left to me!

sentences.zh: 跣走，匿樓下。

translations.literal: Barefoot, he fled and hid beneath a stairway.
translations.idiomatic: Barefoot, he fled and hid under a stairway.

sentences.zh: 親將李鈞引挽強三百趨山亭，欲戰，行立伏兵邀斬之。

translations.literal: His personal general Li Jun led three hundred crossbowmen to a hill pavilion intending to fight, but Xingli's ambush intercepted and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: His personal general Li Jun led three hundred crossbowmen to a hill pavilion to fight, but Pei Xingli's ambush cut him down.

sentences.zh: 錡舉家皆哭，左右執錡，裹之以幕，縋於城下，械送京師。

translations.literal: Qi's whole household wept. His attendants seized Qi, wrapped him in a curtain, lowered him from the city wall by rope, and sent him to the capital in fetters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi's whole household wept. His attendants seized him, wrapped him in a curtain, lowered him from the wall by rope, and sent him to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 挽強、蕃落爭自殺，屍相枕藉。

translations.literal: The crossbowmen and tribal auxiliaries vied to kill themselves; corpses lay piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Crossbowmen and tribal auxiliaries competed to kill themselves; corpses lay piled one on another.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，本軍以聞。

translations.literal: On guiyou day, the local army reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou day the local army reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，群臣賀於紫宸殿。

translations.literal: On yihai day, the ministers offered congratulations in the Zichen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day the ministers offered congratulations in the Zichen Hall.

sentences.zh: 上愀然曰：「朕之不德，致宇内數有干紀者，朕之愧也，何賀之爲！」

translations.literal: The emperor said with a somber face: "My virtue is inadequate, and within the realm rebellion has arisen again and again. I am ashamed—why congratulate me!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said grimly: "My virtue is wanting, and rebellion keeps breaking out across the realm. I am ashamed—what is there to congratulate?"

sentences.zh: 宰相議誅錡大功以上親，兵部郎中蔣乂曰：錡大功親，皆淮安靖王之後也。

translations.literal: The chancellors discussed executing Qi's relatives within the degree of mourning for a great-grandfather. Jiang Yi, director in the Ministry of War, said: "Qi's relatives of that degree are all descendants of Prince Huai of Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors debated executing Li Qi's relatives within the great-grandfather mourning degree. Jiang Yi, a director in the Ministry of War, said: "Li Qi's relatives of that degree are all descendants of Prince Huai of Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 淮安有佐命之功，陪陵、享廟，豈可以末孫爲惡而累之乎！

translations.literal: Huai'an had meritorious service in founding the dynasty, shares the imperial tombs, and receives sacrifices in the ancestral temples—how can we allow a distant descendant's wickedness to stain them!
translations.idiomatic: Huai'an helped found the dynasty, shares the imperial tombs, and receives temple sacrifice—how can a distant descendant's crime be allowed to stain him!

sentences.zh: 又欲誅其兄弟，乂曰：「錡兄弟，故都統國貞之子也，國貞死王事，豈可使之不祀乎！」

translations.literal: They also wished to execute his brothers. Jiang Yi said: "Qi's brothers are sons of the former commander-in-chief Li Guozhen. Guozhen died in the service of the state—how can we let his line go without sacrifice!
translations.idiomatic: They also wanted to execute his brothers. Jiang Yi said: "Li Qi's brothers are sons of the late commander-in-chief Li Guozhen. Guozhen died in imperial service—how can we cut off his sacrifices!

sentences.zh: 宰相以爲然。

translations.literal: The chancellors agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors agreed.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，錡從父弟宋州刺史銛等皆貶官流放。

translations.literal: On xinsi day, Qi's paternal cousin Li Qian, prefect of Songzhou, and others were all demoted and exiled.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day Li Qian, Li Qi's paternal cousin and prefect of Songzhou, and others were demoted and exiled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申朔，錡至長安，上御興安門，面詰之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, jiashen, Qi reached Chang'an. The emperor went to Xing'an Gate and questioned him face to face.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the first day jiashen, Li Qi reached Chang'an. The emperor went to Xing'an Gate and questioned him in person.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣初不反，張子良等教臣耳。」

translations.literal: He answered: "Your subject initially did not rebel. Zhang Ziliang and the others taught me to do it."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I did not rebel at first. Zhang Ziliang and the others put me up to it."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿爲元帥，子良等謀反，何不斬之，然後入朝！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "You were the commander. When Ziliang and the others plotted rebellion, why did you not behead them and then come to court!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You were the commander. When Ziliang and the others plotted rebellion, why did you not behead them and then come to court!

sentences.zh: 錡無以對。

translations.literal: Qi had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 乃並其子師回腰斬之。

translations.literal: Then he and his son Li Shihui were both cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Then he and his son Li Shihui were both executed by waist-slicing.

sentences.zh: 有司請毀錡祖考塚廟，中丞盧坦上言：「李錡父子受誅，罪已塞矣。

translations.literal: The relevant offices requested that Qi's ancestral tombs and shrines be destroyed. Censor Lu Tan submitted a memorial saying: "Li Qi and his son have already been executed; the crime has been answered.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices asked to destroy Li Qi's ancestral tombs and shrines. Censor Lu Tan submitted a memorial: "Li Qi and his son have already been executed; justice has been done.

sentences.zh: 昔漢誅霍禹，不罪霍光；

translations.literal: In former times the Han executed Huo Yu but did not punish Huo Guang;
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Huo Yu was executed, but Huo Guang was not punished;

sentences.zh: 先朝誅房遺愛不及房玄齡。

translations.literal: our preceding dynasty executed Fang Yiai but did not reach Fang Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: in our own dynasty Fang Yiai was executed, but Fang Xuanling was left untouched.

sentences.zh: 《康誥》曰：『父子兄弟，罪不相及。』

translations.literal: The Announcement to Kang says: 'Father and son, elder and younger brother—crimes do not extend to one another.'
translations.idiomatic: The Announcement to Kang says: 'Crimes do not extend from father to son or from elder brother to younger.'

sentences.zh: 以錡爲不善而罪及五代祖乎？」

translations.literal: To punish five generations of ancestors because Qi behaved wickedly?"
translations.idiomatic: Are we to punish five generations of ancestors because Li Qi behaved wickedly?"

sentences.zh: 乃不毀。

translations.literal: The tombs and shrines were therefore not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The tombs and shrines were therefore spared.

sentences.zh: 有司籍錡家財輸京師。

translations.literal: The relevant offices inventoried Qi's family wealth for shipment to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices inventoried Li Qi's family wealth for shipment to the capital.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士裴垍、李絳上言，以爲：「李錡僭侈，割剝六州之人以富其家，或枉殺其身而取其財。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academicians Pei Ji and Li Jiang submitted a memorial arguing: "Li Qi lived beyond his rank and exorbitantly, stripping the people of six prefectures to enrich his household, sometimes killing people unjustly and seizing their property.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academicians Pei Ji and Li Jiang submitted a memorial arguing: "Li Qi lived beyond his station and in extravagance, stripping the people of six prefectures to enrich his house, sometimes killing the innocent to seize their wealth.

sentences.zh: 陛下閔百姓無告，故討而誅之，今輦金帛以輸上京，恐遠近失望。

translations.literal: Your Majesty took pity on the people who had no recourse, and therefore campaigned against him and executed him. Now if you cart gold and silk to the upper capital, I fear those near and far will be disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty took pity on people with no recourse and therefore campaigned against him and executed him. Now to cart gold and silk to the capital would, I fear, disappoint people near and far.

sentences.zh: 願以逆人資財賜浙西百姓，代今年租賦。」

translations.literal: I beg that the rebel's assets be given to the common people of western Zhejiang in place of this year's taxes and levies."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the rebel's assets be given to the people of western Zhejiang in place of this year's taxes and levies."

sentences.zh: 上嘉歎久之，即從其言。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this at length and at once followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised this at length and at once accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使盧從史，内與王士眞、劉濟潛通，而外獻策請圖山東，擅引兵東出。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi, military governor of Zhaoyi, maintained secret ties with Wang Shizhen and Liu Ji while outwardly offering strategies urging an offensive against the Shandong region, and on his own authority led troops eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi, military governor of Zhaoyi, was in secret contact with Wang Shizhen and Liu Ji while outwardly urging a campaign against Shandong, and on his own authority led troops east.

sentences.zh: 上召令還上黨，從史託言就食邢、洺，不時奉詔。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him and ordered him to return to Shangdang. Congshi claimed he was going to Xing and Ming for provisions and did not promptly obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him back to Shangdang, but Congshi claimed he was going to Xing and Ming for provisions and did not obey promptly.

sentences.zh: 久之，乃還。

translations.literal: Only after a long delay did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long delay did he return.

sentences.zh: 他日，上召李絳對於浴堂，語之曰：「事有極異者，朕比不欲言之。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor summoned Li Jiang to converse in the Bath Hall and said to him: "There is something extremely strange. Lately I have not wished to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor summoned Li Jiang to the Bath Hall and said: "There is something very strange. Lately I have not wanted to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 朕與鄭絪議敕從史歸上黨，續征入朝。

translations.literal: I discussed with Zheng Yin ordering Congshi back to Shangdang and then summoning him to court.
translations.idiomatic: I discussed with Zheng Yin ordering Congshi back to Shangdang and then summoning him to court.

sentences.zh: 絪乃洩之於從史，使稱上黨乏糧，就食山東。

translations.literal: Yin then leaked this to Congshi, enabling him to claim that Shangdang lacked grain and that he was going east for provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then leaked this to Congshi, enabling him to claim that Shangdang lacked grain and that he was going east for provisions.

sentences.zh: 爲人臣負朕乃爾，將何以處之？」

translations.literal: For a minister to betray me in this way—what am I to do with him?"
translations.idiomatic: For a minister to betray me like this—what am I to do with him?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「審如此，滅族有餘矣！

translations.literal: Jiang replied: "If that is truly so, even exterminating his clan would not be excessive!
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang replied: "If that is truly so, even exterminating his clan would not be too much!

sentences.zh: 然絪、從史必不自言，陛下誰從得之？」

translations.literal: Yet Yin and Congshi would surely never confess it themselves—whom did Your Majesty hear this from?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yin and Congshi would never confess it themselves—whom did Your Majesty hear this from?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吉甫密奏。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Jifu submitted a secret memorial."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Jifu submitted a secret memorial."

sentences.zh: 絳曰：「臣竊聞搢紳之論，稱絪爲佳士，恐必不然。

translations.literal: Jiang said: "Your subject has privately heard officials discuss Yin and call him an excellent man. I fear that cannot be so.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang said: "I have privately heard officials praise Yin as an excellent man. I fear that cannot be so.

sentences.zh: 或者同列欲專朝政，疾寵忌前，願陛下更熟察之，勿使人謂陛下信讒也！」

translations.literal: Perhaps a colleague wishes to monopolize court affairs, envying favor and hating a predecessor. I beg Your Majesty to examine this more carefully and not let people say Your Majesty trusts slander!"
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps a colleague wishes to monopolize court affairs, envying his rival's favor. I beg Your Majesty to look into this more carefully and not let people say you trust slander!"

sentences.zh: 上良久曰：「誠然，絪必不至此。

translations.literal: After a long pause the emperor said: "That is true. Yin would surely not go so far.
translations.idiomatic: After a long pause the emperor said: "That is true. Yin would surely not go so far.

sentences.zh: 非卿言，朕幾誤處分。」

translations.literal: Had it not been for your words, I would nearly have punished him wrongly."
translations.idiomatic: Had it not been for your words, I would almost have punished him wrongly."

sentences.zh: 上又嘗從容問絳曰：「諫官多謗訕朝政，皆無事實，朕欲謫其尤者一二人以儆其餘，何如？」

translations.literal: The emperor also once casually asked Jiang: "Remonstrating officials often mock and revile court policy, and none of it has factual basis. I wish to demote one or two of the worst as a warning to the rest—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also once casually asked Li Jiang: "Remonstrating officials often mock court policy without factual basis. I wish to demote one or two of the worst as a warning to the rest—what do you think?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此殆非陛下之意，必有邪臣欲壅蔽陛下之聰明者。

translations.literal: He replied: "This is probably not truly Your Majesty's intent. There must be an evil minister who wishes to block and blind Your Majesty's intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "This is probably not truly Your Majesty's intent. Some evil minister must wish to block and blind your intelligence.

sentences.zh: 人臣死生，系人主喜怒，敢發口諫者有幾！

translations.literal: A subject's life and death hang on the sovereign's pleasure or anger—how many would dare open their mouths to remonstrate!
translations.idiomatic: A subject's life and death hang on the sovereign's pleasure or anger—how many would dare speak out in remonstrance!

sentences.zh: 就有諫者皆晝度夜思，朝刪暮減，比得上達，什無二三。

translations.literal: Even when there are remonstrances, each is weighed by day and brooded over by night, trimmed in the morning and cut back in the evening. By the time they reach Your Majesty, not two or three in ten remain.
translations.idiomatic: Even when remonstrances are offered, each is weighed by day and brooded over by night, trimmed in the morning and cut back in the evening. By the time they reach Your Majesty, not two or three in ten remain.

sentences.zh: 故人主孜孜求諫，猶懼不至，況罪之乎！

translations.literal: Therefore a ruler who diligently seeks remonstrance still fears it will not come—how much more if he punishes it!
translations.idiomatic: A ruler who diligently seeks remonstrance still fears it will not come—how much more if he punishes it!

sentences.zh: 如此，杜天下之口，非社稷之福也。」

translations.literal: To do this is to stop up the mouths of the realm—not a blessing for the state."
translations.idiomatic: To do this is to stop up the mouths of the realm—not a blessing for the state."

sentences.zh: 上善其言而止。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved of his words and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved of his advice and desisted.

sentences.zh: 群臣請上尊號曰睿聖文武皇帝，丙申，許之。

translations.literal: The ministers requested that the Emperor take the honorific title Sagacious and Sage, Martial and Cultured Emperor; on bingchen day, he assented.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials asked the Emperor to adopt the honorific title Sagacious and Sage, Martial and Cultured Emperor; on the bingchen day he agreed.

sentences.zh: 盩厔尉、集賢校理白居易作樂府及詩百餘篇，規諷時事，流聞禁中。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi, assistant magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, composed more than a hundred yuefu poems and lyrics satirizing current affairs; they circulated and reached the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi, assistant magistrate of Zhouzhi and collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, wrote more than a hundred yuefu poems and verses criticizing current affairs; news of them reached the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 上風而悅之，召入翰林爲學士。

translations.literal: The Emperor heard of them by repute and was delighted; he summoned Bai into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor heard of them and was delighted; he summoned Bai into the Hanlin Academy as an academician.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙辰，上謂宰相曰：「太宗以神聖之資，群臣進諫者猶往複數四，況朕寡昧，自今事有違，卿當十論，無但一二而已。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on bingchen day, the Emperor said to the Grand Councilors: "Emperor Taizong, with his divine and sage endowment, still had ministers who remonstrated again and again; how much more so for me, who am meager and dull. From now on, whenever something is amiss, you must remonstrate ten times over—not just once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the bingchen day, the Emperor told the Grand Councilors: "Emperor Taizong, endowed with divine wisdom, still heard remonstrance from his ministers again and again—how much more should you speak plainly to me, who am far less capable. From now on, whenever something is wrong, remonstrate fully; do not stop at one or two objections.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以髙崇文同平章事，充邠寧節度、京西諸軍都統。

translations.literal: On bingyin day, Gao Chongwen was appointed Grand Councilor and made military governor of Binning and overall commander of the armies of Jingxi.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingyin day, Gao Chongwen was made Grand Councilor and assigned as military governor of Binning and overall commander of the Jingxi armies.

sentences.zh: 山南東道節度使于頔憚上英威，爲子季友求尚主。

translations.literal: Yu Di, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, feared the Emperor's imposing authority and sought a royal marriage for his son Jiyou.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Di, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, awed by the Emperor's authority, sought an imperial marriage for his son Jiyou.

sentences.zh: 上以皇女普寧公主妻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor gave him the Princess Puning in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor gave his daughter, Princess Puning, to Jiyou in marriage.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳曰：「頔，虜族，季友，庶孽，不足以辱帝女，宜更擇髙門美才。」

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Li Jiang said: "Di is of barbarian stock, and Jiyou is a bastard son—they are unworthy to disgrace an imperial daughter; Your Majesty should choose instead from a lofty house and a fine talent."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Li Jiang said: "Di is of barbarian origin, and Jiyou is a bastard son—they are not fit to marry an imperial daughter. Your Majesty should choose a match from a distinguished house and a man of real talent."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此非卿所知。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "This is not something you understand."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "That is not for you to judge."

sentences.zh: 己卯，公主適季友，恩禮甚盛。

translations.literal: On jimao day, the Princess was wedded to Jiyou with lavish favor and ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day the Princess was married to Jiyou, with extraordinary honors and ceremony.

sentences.zh: 頔出望外，大喜。

translations.literal: Di, utterly beyond his expectations, was overjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Di, utterly beyond his hopes, was overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 頃之，上使人諷之入朝謝恩，頔遂奉詔。

translations.literal: Before long, the Emperor sent word hinting that he should come to court to give thanks for the grace; Di thereupon obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Emperor sent a hint that Di should come to court to give thanks; Di then obeyed the summons.

sentences.zh: 是歳，李吉甫撰《元和國計簿》上之，總計天下方鎭四十八，州府二百九十五，縣千四百五十三。

translations.literal: That year, Li Jifu compiled the Yuanhe Register of State Revenue and submitted it. In total there were forty-eight frontier commands, two hundred ninety-five prefectures, and one thousand four hundred fifty-three counties.
translations.idiomatic: That year Li Jifu compiled the Yuanhe Register of State Revenue and submitted it. All told, the realm had forty-eight frontier commands, two hundred ninety-five prefectures, and one thousand four hundred fifty-three counties.

sentences.zh: 其鳳翔、鄜坊、邠寧、振武、涇原、銀夏、靈鹽、河東、易定、魏博、鎭冀、范陽、滄景、淮西、淄靑等十五道七十一州不申戸口外，毎歳賦稅倚辦止於浙江東、西、宣歙、淮南、江西、鄂岳、福建、湖南八道四十九州，一百四十四萬戸，比天寶稅戸四分減三。

translations.literal: Apart from the fifteen circuits and seventy-one prefectures—Fengxiang, Zheyuan, Binning, Zhenwu, Jingyuan, Yin-Xia, Lingyan, Hedong, Yiding, Weibo, Zhenji, Fanyang, Cangjing, Huaixi, Ziqing, and the like—that did not report household registers, each year's tax revenue had to be procured from only the eight circuits of forty-nine prefectures east and west of Zhejiang, Xuan-She, Huainan, Jiangxi, E-Yue, Fujian, and Hunan: 1,440,000 households—a reduction of three-quarters from the Tianbao tax registers.
translations.idiomatic: Setting aside the fifteen circuits and seventy-one prefectures—including Fengxiang, Zheyuan, Binning, Zhenwu, Jingyuan, Yin-Xia, Lingyan, Hedong, Yiding, Weibo, Zhenji, Fanyang, Cangjing, Huaixi, and Ziqing—that did not report household registers, the empire's annual tax revenue had to be raised from only eight circuits and forty-nine prefectures: Zhejiang East and West, Xuan-She, Huainan, Jiangxi, E-Yue, Fujian, and Hunan. That came to 1,440,000 households—three-quarters fewer than under the Tianbao tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 天下兵仰給縣官者八十三萬餘人，比天寶三分增一，大率二戸資一兵。

translations.literal: Soldiers throughout the realm dependent on the state for provisions numbered more than 830,000—an increase of one-third over Tianbao; on average, two households supported one soldier.
translations.idiomatic: More than 830,000 soldiers across the empire depended on the state for their upkeep—one-third more than in the Tianbao era. On average, two households had to support one soldier.

sentences.zh: 其水旱所傷，非時調發，不在此數。

translations.literal: Flood, drought, and other damage, as well as extraordinary levies and deployments, are not included in these figures.
translations.idiomatic: Damage from flood and drought, and extraordinary levies and deployments, are not counted in these totals.

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳，群臣上尊號曰睿聖文武皇帝；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on guisi day, the ministers offered the honorific title Sagacious and Sage, Martial and Cultured Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month, the guisi day, the court offered the honorific title Sagacious and Sage, Martial and Cultured Emperor;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: He proclaimed amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 「自今長吏詣闕，無得進奉。」

translations.literal: "From now on, when senior officials come to court, they must not make tribute offerings."
translations.idiomatic: "From now on, when senior officials come to court, they must not present tribute offerings."

sentences.zh: 知樞密劉光琦奏分遣中使繼赦詣諸道，意欲分其饋遺，翰林學士裴垍、李絳奏「敕使所至煩擾，不若但附急遞。」

translations.literal: Director of Palace Affairs Liu Guangqi memorialized that eunuchs should be dispatched in succession to carry the amnesty to the various circuits, intending to share in their gifts of gratitude; Hanlin academicians Pei Ji and Li Jiang memorialized: "Wherever imperial envoys go they cause harassment—it would be better simply to send the edict by urgent relay."
translations.idiomatic: Director of Palace Affairs Liu Guangqi proposed dispatching eunuchs in succession to carry the amnesty to the various circuits, intending to share in the gifts they would receive. Hanlin academicians Pei Ji and Li Jiang memorialized: "Wherever imperial envoys go they cause trouble—it would be better simply to send the edict by urgent relay."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 光琦稱舊例，上曰：「例是則從之，苟爲非是，奈何不改！」

translations.literal: Guangqi cited precedent; the Emperor said: "If the precedent is correct, follow it; if it is wrong, why not change it!"
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi cited precedent, but the Emperor said: "If precedent is right, follow it; if it is wrong, why not change it?"

sentences.zh: 臨涇鎭將郝泚以臨涇地險要，水草美，吐蕃將入寇，必屯其地，言於涇原節度使段祐，奏而城之，自是涇原獲安。

translations.literal: The Linjing garrison commander Hao Zhi, because the Linjing region was strategically vital and its pastures and water excellent—and because whenever the Tibetans planned to invade they would always encamp there—spoke to Duan You, military governor of Jingyuan, memorialized, and fortified it; from that time Jingyuan enjoyed peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Zhi, commander of the Linjing garrison, argued that Linjing was strategically vital, with fine pastures and water, and that the Tibetans always encamped there before invading. He persuaded Duan You, military governor of Jingyuan, to memorialize and build a fort there; from then on Jingyuan was secure.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊寅，咸安大長公主薨於回鶻。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuyin day, the Princess Xian'an the Great Long Married died in Uyghur lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the wuyin day, the Princess Xian'an the Great Long Married died among the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 三月，回鶻騰裡可汗卒。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Uyghur Tengli Khan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Uyghur Tengli Khan died.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，郇王總薨。

translations.literal: On guisi day, Prince Xun of Yun died.
translations.idiomatic: On the guisi day Prince Xun of Yun died.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，御史中丞盧坦奏彈前山南西道節度使柳晟，前浙東觀察使閻濟美違赦進奉。

translations.literal: On xinhai day, Chief Censor Lu Tan memorialized impeaching Liu Sheng, former military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and Yan Jimei, former observation commissioner of Zhedong, for violating the amnesty with tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day Chief Censor Lu Tan impeached Liu Sheng, former military governor of Shannan West Circuit, and Yan Jimei, former observation commissioner of Zhedong, for making tribute offerings in violation of the amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上召坦褒慰之，曰：「朕已釋其罪，不可失信。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Tan and praised and comforted him, saying: "I have already pardoned their crime; I cannot break my word."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Tan, praised and comforted him, and said: "I have already pardoned them; I cannot go back on my word."

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「赦令宣佈海内，陛下之大信也。

translations.literal: Tan said: "The amnesty edict has been proclaimed throughout the realm—that is Your Majesty's great pledge of faith.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "The amnesty has been proclaimed throughout the realm—that is Your Majesty's great pledge of faith.

sentences.zh: 晟等不畏陛下法，奈何存小信棄大信乎！」

translations.literal: Sheng and the others did not fear Your Majesty's law—why preserve a small faith and abandon a great faith!"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng and the others showed no fear of Your Majesty's law—why keep a small promise and break a great one!"

sentences.zh: 上乃命歸所進於有司。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon ordered that what they had offered be returned to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then ordered their offerings returned to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，上策試賢良方正直言極諫舉人，伊闕尉牛僧孺、陸渾尉皇甫湜、前進士李宗閔皆指陳時政之失，無所避；

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, the Emperor held an examination for candidates in Worthy, Upright, and Outspoken Extreme Remonstrance; Niu Sengru, magistrate of Yique; Huangfu Shi, magistrate of Luhun; and the former jinshi Li Zongmin all pointed out failings in current policy without evasion;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, the Emperor examined candidates for Worthy, Upright, and Outspoken Extreme Remonstrance. Niu Sengru, magistrate of Yique; Huangfu Shi, magistrate of Luhun; and the former jinshi Li Zongmin all criticized current policy frankly, without holding back;

sentences.zh: 戸部侍郎楊於陵、吏部員外郎韋貫之爲考策官，貫之署爲上第。

translations.literal: Yang Yuling, vice minister of revenue, and Wei Guanzhi, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, served as examiners; Guanzhi ranked them in the top grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling, vice minister of revenue, and Wei Guanzhi, vice director in the Ministry of Personnel, served as examiners; Guanzhi placed them in the top grade.

sentences.zh: 上亦嘉之。

translations.literal: The Emperor also commended them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also praised them.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，詔中書優與處分。

translations.literal: On yichou day, an edict ordered the Secretariat to favor them with appointments.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day an edict directed the Secretariat to grant them favorable appointments.

sentences.zh: 李吉甫惡其言直，泣訴於上，且言「翰林學士裴垍、王涯覆策。

translations.literal: Li Jifu hated their forthright words, wept and complained to the Emperor, and also said: "Hanlin academicians Pei Ji and Wang Ya reviewed the examination papers.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu resented their blunt criticism, wept and complained to the Emperor, and also said: "Hanlin academicians Pei Ji and Wang Ya reviewed the examination papers.

sentences.zh: 湜，涯之甥也，涯不先言；

translations.literal: Shi is Wang Ya's nephew, and Ya did not declare this beforehand;
translations.idiomatic: Shi was Wang Ya's nephew, yet Ya had not disclosed this beforehand;

sentences.zh: 垍無所異同。」

translations.literal: Pei Ji raised no objection."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji raised no objection.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，罷垍、涯學士，垍爲戸部侍郎，涯爲都官員外郎，貫之爲果州刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no choice, dismissed Pei Ji and Ya from their Hanlin posts; Pei Ji became vice minister of revenue, Ya became vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guanzhi became prefect of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, having no choice, removed Pei Ji and Ya from the Hanlin Academy. Pei Ji was made vice minister of revenue, Ya vice director in the Ministry of Justice, and Guanzhi prefect of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 後數日，費之再貶巴州刺史，涯貶虢州司馬。

translations.literal: Several days later, Guanzhi was demoted again to prefect of Bazhou, and Ya was demoted to secretary of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Guanzhi was demoted again to prefect of Bazhou, and Ya was demoted to secretary of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以楊於陵爲嶺南節度使，亦坐考策無異同也。

translations.literal: On yihai day, Yang Yuling was made military governor of Lingnan—also for having graded the examination papers without dissent.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day Yang Yuling was made military governor of Lingnan—also punished for grading the examination without dissent.

sentences.zh: 僧孺等久之不調，各從辟於籓府。

translations.literal: Sengru and the others long went without appointments and each accepted positions as staff members in frontier commands.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru and the others went long without court appointments and each entered service in a frontier command.

sentences.zh: 僧孺，弘之七世孫；

translations.literal: Sengru was the seventh-generation descendant of Niu Hong;
translations.idiomatic: Sengru was a seventh-generation descendant of Niu Hong;

sentences.zh: 宗閔，元懿之玄孫；

translations.literal: Zongmin was the great-great-grandson of Li Yuanyi;
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin was a great-great-grandson of Li Yuanyi;

sentences.zh: 貫之，福嗣之六世孫；

translations.literal: Guanzhi was the sixth-generation descendant of Wei Fusi;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhi was a sixth-generation descendant of Wei Fusi;

sentences.zh: 湜，睦州新安人也。

translations.literal: Shi was a native of Xin'an in Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was a native of Xin'an in Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，罷五月朔宣政殿朝賀。

translations.literal: On dingchou day, the first-day court audience and congratulations at Xuanzheng Hall in the fifth month were suspended.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingchou day the first-day court audience and congratulations at Xuanzheng Hall in the fifth month were canceled.

sentences.zh: 以荊南節度使裴均爲右僕射。

translations.literal: Pei Jun, military governor of Jingnan, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, military governor of Jingnan, was appointed Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 均素附宦官得貴顯，爲僕射，自矜大。

translations.literal: Jun had always relied on eunuchs to gain wealth and eminence; as Vice Director, he was greatly self-important.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had long curried favor with eunuchs to rise in wealth and rank; as Vice Director he became insufferably proud.

sentences.zh: 嘗入朝，逾位而立；

translations.literal: Once when he entered court, he stood beyond his proper place in the ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Once when he attended court he stood out of his proper place in the ranks;

sentences.zh: 中丞盧坦揖而退之，均不從。

translations.literal: Chief Censor Lu Tan bowed and withdrew him, but Jun would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Censor Lu Tan bowed and tried to move him back, but Jun refused.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「昔姚南仲爲僕射，位在此。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "In former times Yao Nanyong as Vice Director stood in this place."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "In former times, when Yao Nanyong was Vice Director, he stood here."

sentences.zh: 均曰：「南仲何人？」

translations.literal: Jun said: "Who was Nanyong?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "Who was Nanyong?"

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「是守正不交權幸者。」

translations.literal: Tan said: "He was one who upheld integrity and would not consort with the powerful and favored."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "A man who kept his integrity and would not consort with the powerful and favored."

sentences.zh: 坦尋改右庶子。

translations.literal: Before long Tan was transferred to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Tan was transferred to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 五月，翰林學士、左拾遺白居易上疎，以爲：「牛僧孺等直言時事，恩獎登科，而更遭斥逐，並出爲關外官。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Hanlin academician and Left Remonstrance Censor Bai Juyi submitted a memorial, stating: "Niu Sengru and the others spoke frankly on current affairs, were rewarded with passing the examination, yet were then driven away—all sent out to posts beyond the passes as officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Hanlin academician and Left Remonstrance Censor Bai Juyi submitted a memorial arguing: "Niu Sengru and the others spoke frankly on current affairs, were rewarded with passing the examination, and were then driven out—all sent to posts beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 楊於陵等以考策敢收直言，裴□等以覆策不退直言，皆坐譴謫。

translations.literal: Yang Yuling and the others were punished for daring to accept frank speech in grading the examination; Pei Ji and the others were punished for not suppressing frank speech when reviewing the papers—all were demoted and banished.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yuling and the others were punished for daring to accept frank answers in the examination; Pei Ji and the others were punished for not suppressing frank speech when reviewing the papers—all were demoted and banished.

sentences.zh: 盧坦以數舉職事黜庶子。

translations.literal: Lu Tan was demoted to Subordinate of the Heir Apparent for repeatedly performing his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan was demoted to Subordinate of the Heir Apparent for repeatedly doing his duty.

sentences.zh: 此數人皆今之人望，天下視其進退以卜時之否藏者也。

translations.literal: These several men are the hope of the age; the realm looks to their advancement or removal to foretell whether the times are good or ill.
translations.idiomatic: These men are the hope of the age; the realm watches their rise and fall to read whether the times are good or ill.

sentences.zh: 一旦無罪悉疎棄之，上下杜口，衆心洶湧，陛下亦知之乎？

translations.literal: Yet in a single stroke they were all cast aside though guiltless; above and below mouths were stopped, popular sentiment surged—in does Your Majesty know this?
translations.idiomatic: Yet in one stroke they were all cast aside though guiltless; above and below people fell silent, popular sentiment surged—does Your Majesty know this?

sentences.zh: 且陛下既下詔征之直言，索之極諫，僧孺等所對如此，縱未能推而行之，又何忍罪而斥之乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty both issued an edict summoning frank speech and seeking extreme remonstrance; Sengru and the others answered thus—even if you could not push forward and implement it, how could you bear to punish and banish them!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty issued an edict calling for frank speech and extreme remonstrance; Sengru and the others answered as they did—even if you could not act on their words, how can you bear to punish and banish them!

sentences.zh: 昔德宗初即位，亦征直言極諫之士，策問天旱，穆質對云：『兩漢故事，三公當免，卜式著議，弘羊可烹。』

translations.literal: In former times when Emperor Dezong first took the throne, he also summoned men of frank and extreme remonstrance; in the examination question on drought, Mu Zhi answered, saying: 'In the stories of the Two Han dynasties, the Three Dukes ought to be dismissed; Bu Shi set forth his opinion, and Sang Hongyang deserved to be boiled alive.'
translations.idiomatic: In former times, when Emperor Dezong first took the throne, he too summoned men of frank and extreme remonstrance. On an examination question about drought, Mu Zhi answered: 'In the stories of the Two Han dynasties, the Three Dukes ought to be dismissed; Bu Shi set forth his opinion, and Sang Hongyang deserved to be boiled alive.

sentences.zh: 德宗深嘉之，自畿尉擢爲左補闕。

translations.literal: Dezong deeply commended him and promoted him from a county aide to Left Supplementation Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong deeply praised him and promoted him from a county aide to Left Supplementation Censor.

sentences.zh: 今僧孺等所言未過於穆質，而遽斥之，臣恐非嗣祖宗之道也！」

translations.literal: Now what Sengru and the others said did not exceed Mu Zhi—and yet they were suddenly banished; I fear this is not the way to continue the path of the ancestors!"
translations.idiomatic: What Sengru and the others said did not go beyond Mu Zhi—yet they were suddenly banished. I fear this is not the way to follow the path of the ancestors!"

sentences.zh: 質，寧之子也。

translations.literal: Zhi was a son of Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Zhi was a son of Mu Ning.

sentences.zh: 丙午，冊回鶻新可汗爲愛登裡囉汨密施合毘伽保義可汗。

translations.literal: On bingwu day, the new Uyghur khan was invested as Khan Aidengli Luomimisihebiqiapoai.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day the new Uyghur khan was invested as Khan Aidengli Luomimisihebiqiapoai.

sentences.zh: 西原蠻酋長黃少卿請降。

translations.literal: Huang Shaoqing, chieftain of the Xiyuan barbarians, requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Shaoqing, chieftain of the Xiyuan tribes, offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸亥，以爲歸順州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on guihai day, he was made prefect of Guishun.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the guihai day, he was appointed prefect of Guishun.

sentences.zh: 沙陀勁勇冠諸胡，吐蕃置之甘州，毎戰，以爲前鋒。

translations.literal: The Shatuo were the fiercest and bravest among all the barbarians; the Tibetans stationed them at Ganzhou, and in every battle used them as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were the fiercest and bravest of the northern peoples; the Tibetans stationed them at Ganzhou and used them as vanguard in every battle.

sentences.zh: 回鶻攻吐蕃，取涼州。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs attacked the Tibetans and took Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs attacked the Tibetans and captured Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃疑沙陀貳於回鶻，欲遷之河外。

translations.literal: The Tibetans suspected the Shatuo of double-dealing with the Uyghurs and intended to move them beyond the river.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans suspected the Shatuo of colluding with the Uyghurs and planned to relocate them beyond the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 沙陀懼，酋長朱邪盡忠與其子執宜謀復自歸於唐，遂帥部落三萬，循烏德犍山而東。

translations.literal: The Shatuo were afraid; their chieftain Zhuye Jinzhong and his son Zhuoci plotted to return to allegiance to Tang, and led their tribe of thirty thousand along Wudejian Mountain eastward.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo were afraid. Their chieftain Zhuye Jinzhong and his son Zhuoci plotted to return to Tang allegiance and led their tribe of thirty thousand east along Wudejian Mountain.

sentences.zh: 行三日，吐蕃追兵大至，自洮水轉戰至石門，凡數百合。

translations.literal: After three days' march, Tibetan pursuers arrived in force; from fighting at the Tao River they battled onward to Shimen—altogether several score engagements.
translations.idiomatic: After three days' march Tibetan pursuers caught up in force. They fought from the Tao River all the way to Shimen—several score battles in all.

sentences.zh: 盡忠死，士衆死者大半。

translations.literal: Jinzhong died; soldiers and people died to the number of more than half.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhong was killed, and more than half the warriors and people died.

sentences.zh: 執宜帥其餘衆猶近萬人，騎三千，詣靈州降。

translations.literal: Zhuoci led the remaining multitude, still nearly ten thousand strong with three thousand horses, and came to Lingzhou to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuoci led the survivors—still nearly ten thousand people and three thousand horses—to Lingzhou to surrender.

sentences.zh: 靈鹽節度使范希朝聞之，自帥衆迎於塞上，置之鹽州，爲市牛羊，廣其畜牧，善撫之。

translations.literal: Fan Xichao, military governor of Lingyan, heard of it, personally led troops to meet them beyond the frontier, settled them at Yanzhou, purchased cattle and sheep for them, expanded their herding, and treated them well.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Xichao, military governor of Lingyan, heard of it and personally led troops to meet them at the frontier. He settled them at Yanzhou, bought cattle and sheep for them, expanded their herds, and treated them kindly.

sentences.zh: 詔置陰山府，以執宜爲兵馬使。

translations.literal: An edict established the Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhuoci military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict established Yinshan Prefecture and made Zhuoci its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 未幾，盡忠弟葛勒阿波又帥衆七百詣希朝降，詔以爲陰山府都督。

translations.literal: Before long, Jinzhong's younger brother Gele'abo also led seven hundred men to come to Xichao and surrender; an edict made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jinzhong's younger brother Gele'abo also led seven hundred men to surrender to Xichao; an edict made him governor of Yinshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自是，靈鹽毎有征討，用之所向皆捷，靈鹽軍益強。

translations.literal: From this time on, whenever Lingyan sent out campaigns, employing them they were victorious wherever they went, and Lingyan's army grew stronger.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, whenever Lingyan went on campaign and employed them, they were victorious wherever they went, and Lingyan's army grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛已朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day xinsi there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, on the first day of the seventh month, the xinsi day, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 以右庶子盧坦爲宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Lu Tan, Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, was made observation commissioner of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan, Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent, was made observation commissioner of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 蘇強之誅也，兄弘在晉州幕府，自免歸，人莫敢辟。

translations.literal: When Su Qiang was executed, his elder brother Su Hong was in the staff of Jinzhou; he resigned and returned home, and no one dared to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Qiang was executed, his elder brother Su Hong was serving on the staff at Jinzhou. He resigned and returned home, and no one dared to hire him.

sentences.zh: 坦奏：「弘有才行，不可以其弟故廢之，請闢爲判官。」

translations.literal: Tan memorialized: "Hong has talent and conduct; he cannot be dismissed because of his younger brother's offense—I request that he be recruited as administrative aide."
translations.idiomatic: Tan memorialized: "Hong has talent and character; he should not be discarded because of his brother's crime. I ask that he be recruited as my administrative aide."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「向使蘇強不死，果有才行，猶可用也，況其兄乎！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "If in the past Su Qiang had not been put to death, and he truly had talent and conduct, he could still have been used—how much more so his elder brother!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "If Su Qiang had not been executed, and he truly had talent and character, he could still have been used—how much more so his elder brother!"

sentences.zh: 坦到官，値旱饑，谷價日增，或請抑其價。

translations.literal: When Tan took up his post, there was drought and famine; grain prices rose daily, and some suggested suppressing the price.
translations.idiomatic: When Tan took up his post there was drought and famine; grain prices rose daily, and some suggested forcing prices down.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「宣、歙土狹谷少，所仰四方之來者。

translations.literal: Tan said: "Xuan and She have narrow land and little grain; they depend on supplies coming from all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: "Xuan and She have little land and little grain; they depend on supplies brought in from elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 若價賤，則商船不復來，益困矣。」

translations.literal: If prices are low, then merchant ships will not come again, and the hardship will grow worse."
translations.idiomatic: If prices are kept low, merchant ships will not come, and the hardship will only grow worse."

sentences.zh: 既而米斗二百，商旅輻湊，民賴以生。

translations.literal: Before long, rice reached two hundred cash per dou, and merchants and travelers converged; the people relied on this to survive.
translations.idiomatic: Before long rice reached two hundred cash per dou; merchants and travelers converged, and the people survived on the trade.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚寅，以於于頔爲司空，同平章事如故；

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengyin day, Yu Di was made Minister of Works, remaining Grand Councilor as before;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the gengyin day, Yu Di was made Minister of Works while remaining Grand Councilor as before;

sentences.zh: 加右僕射裴均同平章事，爲山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Pei Jun, Right Vice Director, was made Grand Councilor and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Jun, Right Vice Director, was made Grand Councilor and military governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使王鍔入朝。

translations.literal: Wang E, military governor of Huainan, came to court.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E, military governor of Huainan, came to court.

sentences.zh: 鍔家巨富，厚進奉及賂宦官，求平章事。

translations.literal: E's family was immensely wealthy; he made heavy tribute offerings and bribed eunuchs, seeking to become Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang E's family was immensely wealthy; he made lavish tribute offerings and bribed eunuchs, seeking the post of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士白居易上言以爲：「宰相人臣極位，非淸望大功不應授。

translations.literal: Hanlin academician Bai Juyi submitted a memorial stating: "Grand Councilor is the highest post among ministers; it should not be granted except to men of pure repute and great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academician Bai Juyi submitted a memorial arguing: "Grand Councilor is the highest office a minister can hold; it should be granted only to men of pure reputation and great achievement.

sentences.zh: 昨除裴均，外議已紛然，今又除鍔，則如鍔之輩皆生冀望。

translations.literal: Yesterday Pei Jun was appointed, and criticism outside court was already noisy; now if E is also appointed, then men like E will all be filled with hope.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Jun was appointed yesterday, criticism outside court was already loud; if Wang E is appointed now, then men like him will all be filled with hope.

sentences.zh: 若盡與之，則典章大懷，又不感恩；

translations.literal: If all are granted the post, then the standards of office will be greatly violated, and they will not be grateful;
translations.idiomatic: If all such men are granted the post, the standards of office will be greatly violated, and they will not feel grateful;

sentences.zh: 不與，則厚薄有殊，或生怨望。

translations.literal: If they are not granted, then favor will be uneven, and resentment may arise.
translations.idiomatic: If they are not granted it, favor will seem uneven, and resentment may arise.

sentences.zh: 幸門一啓，無可如何。

translations.literal: Once that gate of fortune is opened, there is no remedy.
translations.idiomatic: Once that gate of favor is opened, there will be no remedy.

sentences.zh: 且鍔在鎭五年，百計誅求，貨財既足，自入進奉。

translations.literal: Moreover, E has been in his command for five years, devising every scheme to extort; once his wealth was sufficient, he came in person to make tribute offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Wang E has been in his command for five years, devising every scheme to extort wealth; once his coffers were full, he came to court in person to make tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 若除宰相，四方籓鎭皆謂鍔以進奉得之，競爲割剝，則百姓何以堪之！」

translations.literal: If he is made Grand Councilor, the buffer regions in all four directions will all say that E obtained the post through tribute offerings, and will compete in plunder and exploitation—how can the common people bear it!"
translations.idiomatic: If Wang E is made Grand Councilor, every buffer region will conclude that he won the post through tribute offerings and will compete in plunder and exploitation. How could the common people endure it!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was then dropped.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，加宣武節度使韓弘同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Han Hong, military governor of Xuanwu, was additionally made Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, Han Hong, military governor of Xuanwu, was additionally made Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 丙申，以戸部侍郎裴垍爲中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, Pei Ji, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, Pei Ji, Vice Minister of Revenue, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 上雖以李吉甫故罷垍學士，然寵信彌厚，故未幾復擢爲相。

translations.literal: Although the Emperor had removed Ji from the Hanlin Academy because of Li Jifu, his favor and trust grew ever deeper, and before long Ji was again promoted to chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Emperor had removed Pei Ji from the Hanlin Academy because of Li Jifu, his favor and trust only deepened, and before long Pei Ji was again promoted to chancellor.

sentences.zh: 初，德宗不任宰相，天下細務皆自決之，由是裴延齡輩得用事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Dezong did not rely on his chancellors; he decided all minor affairs throughout the realm himself, and thus men like Pei Yanling were able to wield power.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Emperor Dezong did not rely on his chancellors and decided every minor affair throughout the realm himself, which allowed men like Pei Yanling to wield power.

sentences.zh: 上在籓邸，心固非之，及即位，選擢宰相，推心委之，嘗謂□等曰：「以太宗、玄宗之明，猶藉輔佐以成其理，況如朕不及先聖萬倍者乎！」

translations.literal: When the Emperor was in his princely residence, he had inwardly disapproved of this; once he took the throne, he selected and promoted chancellors and entrusted them with his whole heart. He once told his chancellors: "With the brilliance of Taizong and Xuanzong, they still relied on assistants to bring their rule to completion—how much more so for one like me, who falls short of the former sages by ten thousandfold!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was still in his princely residence, he had inwardly disapproved of this. Once he took the throne, he selected and promoted chancellors and entrusted them with his whole heart. He once told his chancellors: "Even with the brilliance of Taizong and Xuanzong, they still relied on assistants to bring their rule to completion—how much more so for one like me, who falls short of the former sages by ten thousandfold!"

sentences.zh: 垍亦竭誠輔佐。

translations.literal: Ji also devoted himself wholeheartedly to assisting him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji also devoted himself wholeheartedly to assisting him.

sentences.zh: 上嘗問□：「爲理之要何先？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once asked Ji: "In governing, what should come first?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once asked Pei Ji: "In governing, what should come first?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「先正其心。」

translations.literal: He replied: "First rectify the heart."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "First rectify the heart."

sentences.zh: 舊制，民輸稅有三：一曰上供，二曰送使，三曰留州。

translations.literal: Under the old system, the people's tax payments had three categories: first, tribute to the capital; second, goods sent to the commissioners; third, goods retained by the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, the people's tax payments fell into three categories: tribute to the capital, goods sent to imperial commissioners, and goods retained by the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建中初定兩稅，貨重錢輕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianzhong era the two-tax system was established, when goods were valued highly and cash was cheap.
translations.idiomatic: When the two-tax system was established at the beginning of the Jianzhong era, goods were valued highly and cash was cheap.

sentences.zh: 是後貨輕錢重，民所出已倍其初。

translations.literal: After this, goods were cheap and cash was dear, and what the people paid out had already doubled what it had been at first.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward goods became cheap and cash dear, and what the people paid out had already doubled the original amount.

sentences.zh: 其留州、送使者，所在又降省估，就實估以重斂於民。

translations.literal: As for the goods retained by the prefectures and those sent to commissioners, everywhere officials further lowered the official valuation and, using the actual valuation, heavily levied on the people.
translations.idiomatic: As for goods retained by prefectures and those sent to commissioners, officials everywhere further lowered the official valuation and, using actual market prices, heavily levied on the people.

sentences.zh: 及垍爲相，奏：「天下留州、送使物，請一切用省估。

translations.literal: When Ji became chancellor, he submitted a memorial: "For goods retained by prefectures and sent to commissioners throughout the realm, please use the official valuation for all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Ji became chancellor, he submitted a memorial: "For goods retained by prefectures and sent to commissioners throughout the realm, please apply the official valuation in all cases.

sentences.zh: 其觀察使，先稅所理之州以自給，不足，然後許稅於所屬之州。」

translations.literal: As for observation commissioners, they were first to tax the prefectures they administered to supply themselves; only if that was insufficient were they then permitted to tax the prefectures under their jurisdiction."
translations.idiomatic: Observation commissioners were to tax first the prefectures they directly administered to supply themselves; only if that proved insufficient were they permitted to tax the prefectures under their jurisdiction."

sentences.zh: 由是江、淮之民稍蘇息。

translations.literal: Because of this, the people of the Jiang and Huai regions gradually recovered and rested.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, the people of the Jiang and Huai regions gradually recovered.

sentences.zh: 先是，執政多惡諫官言時政得失，□獨賞之。

translations.literal: Earlier, those in power mostly disliked remonstrating officials who spoke of the gains and losses of current policy, but Ji alone valued them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, those in power mostly disliked remonstrating officials who spoke of current policy's strengths and failings, but Pei Ji alone valued them.

sentences.zh: □器局峻整，人不敢干以私。

translations.literal: Ji's bearing was stern and dignified; no one dared to importune him with private requests.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji's bearing was stern and dignified; no one dared to importune him with private requests.

sentences.zh: 嘗有故人自遠詣之，□資給優厚，從容款狎。

translations.literal: Once an old friend came to visit him from afar; Ji provided him with generous support and received him with easy warmth and familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: Once an old friend came to visit him from afar; Pei Ji provided generous support and received him with easy warmth and familiarity.

sentences.zh: 其人乘間求京兆判司，垍曰：「公才不稱此官，不敢以故人之私傷朝廷至公。

translations.literal: The man seized an opportunity to request a post as assistant magistrate of the capital district. Ji said: "Your talent does not fit this office; I dare not let private friendship with an old acquaintance injure the supreme impartiality of the court.
translations.idiomatic: The man seized an opportunity to request a post as assistant magistrate of the capital district. Pei Ji said: "Your talent does not fit this office; I dare not let private friendship with an old acquaintance injure the court's supreme impartiality.

sentences.zh: 它日有盲宰相憐公者，不妨得之，垍則必不可。」

translations.literal: If someday there is a blind chancellor who takes pity on you, you may still obtain it; as for Ji, that is absolutely impossible."
translations.idiomatic: If someday there is an incompetent chancellor who takes pity on you, you may still obtain it—but not from Pei Ji."

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以中書侍郎、同平章事李吉甫同平章事，充淮南節度使。

translations.literal: On the day wuxu, Li Jifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was made Grand Councilor and assigned as military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu day, Li Jifu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor, was confirmed as Grand Councilor and assigned military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 河中、晉絳節度使邠宣公社黃裳薨。

translations.literal: Du Huangshang, Duke of Bin and military governor of Hezhong and Jin-jiang Circuits, died.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangshang, Duke of Bin and military governor of Hezhong and Jin-jiang Circuits, died.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，庚戌，置行原州於臨涇，以鎭將郝下泚爲刺史。

translations.literal: In winter, the twelfth month, on the day gengxu, a provisional Yuan Prefecture was established at Linjing, and the garrison commander Hao Ci was made its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, on the gengxu day, a provisional Yuan Prefecture was established at Linjing, and the garrison commander Hao Ci was made its prefect.

sentences.zh: 南詔王異牟尋卒，子尋閣勸立。

translations.literal: Yimouxun, king of Nanzhao, died, and his son Xungequan was enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Yimouxun, king of Nanzhao, died, and his son Xungequan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗昭文章武大聖至神孝皇帝上之上元和四年{{*|己丑，西元八〇九年}}

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong — the Illustrious, Literary, Martial, Great, Sage, Supreme, Divine, and Filial — Part One Above, Year Four of Yuanhe (jichou, 809 CE)
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong — the Illustrious, Literary, Martial, Great, Sage, Supreme, Divine, and Filial — Part One Above, Year Four of Yuanhe (809 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子，簡王遘薨。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on the day wuzi, Prince Jian, You, died.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the wuzi day, Prince Jian, You, died.

sentences.zh: 渤海康王嵩璘卒，子元瑜立，改元永德。

translations.literal: Song Lin, King Kang of Bohai, died; his son Yuanyu succeeded him and changed the era name to Yongde.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lin, King Kang of Bohai, died; his son Yuanyu succeeded him and changed the era name to Yongde.

sentences.zh: 南方旱饑。

translations.literal: The south suffered drought and famine.
translations.idiomatic: The south suffered drought and famine.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，命左司郎中鄭敬等爲江、淮、二浙、荊、湖、襄、鄂等道宣慰使，賑恤之，將行，上戒之曰：「朕宮中用帛一匹，皆籍其數，惟貝周救百姓，則不計費，卿輩宜識此意，勿效潘孟陽飲酒遊山而已。」

translations.literal: On the day gengyin, Zheng Jing, Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, and others were appointed pacification commissioners for the Jiang-Huai, Two Zhe, Jing, Hu, Xiang, and E circuits to relieve and succor the people. As they were about to depart, the Emperor admonished them, saying: "In my palace, every bolt of silk is recorded by number; only when relieving and saving the common people do I disregard expense. You should understand this intent and not imitate Pan Mengyang, who merely drank wine and toured the mountains."
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day, Zheng Jing, Left Director of the Department of State Affairs, and others were appointed pacification commissioners for the Jiang-Huai, Two Zhe, Jing, Hu, Xiang, and E circuits to relieve the people. As they were about to depart, the Emperor admonished them: "In my palace, every bolt of silk is recorded by number; only when relieving and saving the common people do I disregard expense. You should understand this intent and not imitate Pan Mengyang, who merely drank wine and toured the mountains."

sentences.zh: 給事中李籓在門下，制敕有不可者，即於黃紙後批之。

translations.literal: Li Fan, Supervising Secretary in the Chancellery, whenever an edict was unacceptable would immediately annotate it on the yellow paper behind it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fan, Supervising Secretary in the Chancellery, would immediately annotate any unacceptable edict on the yellow paper behind it.

sentences.zh: 吏請更連素紙，籓曰：「如此，乃狀也，何名批敕！」

translations.literal: The clerks asked to attach fresh white paper, but Fan said: "If it were done that way, it would be a formal memorial—what would be the point of annotating an edict!"
translations.idiomatic: The clerks asked to attach fresh white paper, but Fan said: "If it were done that way, it would be a formal memorial—what would be the point of annotating an edict!"

sentences.zh: 裴垍薦籓有宰相器。

translations.literal: Pei Ji recommended Fan as having the makings of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji recommended Fan as having the makings of a chancellor.

sentences.zh: 上以門下侍郎、同平章事鄭絪循默取容，二月，丁卯，罷絪爲太子賓客，擢籓爲門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Zheng Yin, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, compliant and silent in currying favor. In the second month, on the day dingmao, Yin was removed and made Advisor to the Heir Apparent, and Fan was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor considered Zheng Yin, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor, overly compliant and silent in currying favor. In the second month, on the dingmao day, Yin was removed and made Advisor to the Heir Apparent, and Fan was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 籓知無不言，上甚重之。

translations.literal: Fan spoke out on everything he knew, and the Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Fan spoke out on everything he knew, and the Emperor greatly valued him.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使嚴綬，在鎭九年，軍政補署一出監軍李輔光，綬拱手而已。

translations.literal: Yan Shou, military governor of Hedong, had been in his command for nine years; all military and administrative appointments came solely from the army supervisor Li Fuguang, and Shou merely folded his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shou, military governor of Hedong, had been in his command for nine years; all military and administrative appointments came solely from the army supervisor Li Fuguang, while Shou merely folded his hands.

sentences.zh: 裴垍具奏其狀，請以李鄘代之。

translations.literal: Pei Ji fully memorialized the situation and requested that Li Yun replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji fully memorialized the situation and requested that Li Yun replace him.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙酉，以綬爲左僕射，以鳳翔節度使李鄘爲河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, on the day yiyou, Shou was made Left Vice Director, and Li Yun, military governor of Fengxiang, was made military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the yiyou day, Shou was made Left Vice Director, and Li Yun, military governor of Fengxiang, was made military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使王士眞薨，其子副大使承宗自爲留後。

translations.literal: Wang Shizhen, military governor of Chengde, died, and his son, the vice commissioner, Chengzong, made himself acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shizhen, military governor of Chengde, died, and his son Chengzong, the vice commissioner, made himself acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 河北三鎭，相承各置副大使，以嫡長爲之，父沒則代領軍務。

translations.literal: The three Hebei buffer regions each successively established vice commissioners, appointing the eldest legitimate son to the post; when the father died, he would succeed to command of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The three Hebei buffer regions each established vice commissioners, appointing the eldest legitimate son; when the father died, the son would succeed to command of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 上以久旱，欲降德音。

translations.literal: Because of the long drought, the Emperor wished to issue a benevolent edict.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the long drought, the Emperor wished to issue a benevolent edict.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳、白居易上言，以爲「欲令實惠及人，無如減其租稅。」

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Bai Juyi submitted memorials, stating: "If one wishes to bring real benefit to the people, nothing is better than reducing their rent and taxes."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and Bai Juyi submitted memorials arguing: "If one wishes to bring real benefit to the people, nothing is better than reducing their rent and taxes."

sentences.zh: 又言「宮人驅使之餘，其數猶廣，事宜省費，物貴徇情。」

translations.literal: They also said: "Even after the palace women needed for service are counted, their number is still large; affairs should be conducted with reduced expense, and goods should be valued according to genuine need."
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "Even after counting the palace women needed for service, their number is still large; affairs should be conducted with reduced expense, and goods should be valued according to genuine need."

sentences.zh: 又請「禁諸道橫斂，以充進奉。」

translations.literal: They also requested: "Prohibit the buffer regions from levying arbitrary exactions to supply tribute offerings."
translations.idiomatic: They also requested: "Prohibit the buffer regions from levying arbitrary exactions to supply tribute offerings."

sentences.zh: 又言「嶺南、黔中、福建風俗，多掠良人賣爲奴婢，乞嚴禁止。」

translations.literal: They also said: "In Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Fujian, by custom many free persons are seized and sold as slaves and bondmaids; we beg that this be strictly forbidden."
translations.idiomatic: They also said: "In Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Fujian, by custom many free persons are seized and sold as slaves and bondmaids; we beg that this be strictly forbidden."

sentences.zh: 閏月，己酉，制降天下系囚，蠲租稅，出宮人，絶進奉，禁掠賣，皆如二臣之請。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on the day jiyou, an edict was issued pardoning prisoners throughout the realm, remitting rent and taxes, releasing palace women, ending tribute offerings, and forbidding abduction and sale—all as the two ministers had requested.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on the jiyou day, an edict was issued pardoning prisoners throughout the realm, remitting rent and taxes, releasing palace women, ending tribute offerings, and forbidding abduction and sale—all as the two ministers had requested.

sentences.zh: 己未，雨。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, it rained.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiwei day, it rained.

sentences.zh: 絳表賀曰：「乃知憂先於事，故能無憂；

translations.literal: Jiang submitted a congratulatory memorial, saying: "Thus one knows that if worry comes before events, one can then be without worry;
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiang submitted a congratulatory memorial, saying: "Thus one knows that if worry comes before events, one can then be without worry;

sentences.zh: 事至而憂，無救於事。」

translations.literal: if one worries only after events arrive, there is no remedy for affairs."
translations.idiomatic: if one worries only after events arrive, there is no remedy for affairs."

sentences.zh: 初，王叔文之黨既貶，有詔，雖遇赦無得量移。

translations.literal: Earlier, after the faction of Wang Shuwen had been demoted and banished, there was an edict that even if an amnesty were granted, they were not to be transferred closer to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the faction of Wang Shuwen had been demoted and banished, an edict declared that even if an amnesty were granted, they were not to be transferred closer to the capital.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書、鹽鐵轉運使李巽奏：「郴州司馬程異，吏才明辨，請以爲楊子留後。」

translations.literal: Li Xun, Minister of the Civil Service and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, submitted a memorial: "Cheng Yi, prefectural aide of Chenzhou, is clear and discerning in administrative talent; please appoint him acting commissioner of Yangzi."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, Minister of the Civil Service and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner, submitted a memorial: "Cheng Yi, prefectural aide of Chenzhou, is clear and discerning in administrative talent; please appoint him acting commissioner of Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 巽精於督察，吏人居千里之外，戰慄如在巽前。

translations.literal: Xun was skilled at supervision and inspection; officials living a thousand li away trembled as if they were before Xun himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was skilled at supervision and inspection; officials living a thousand li away trembled as if they stood before Xun himself.

sentences.zh: 異句檢簿籍，又精於巽，卒獲其用。

translations.literal: Yi examined and checked the ledgers line by line and was even more skilled than Xun; in the end he proved useful to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi examined and checked the ledgers line by line and was even more skilled than Xun; in the end he proved indispensable.

sentences.zh: 魏徴玄孫稠貧甚，以故第質錢於人，平盧節度使李師道請以私財贖出之。

translations.literal: Chou, a great-great-grandson of Wei Zheng, was extremely poor and had pawned the family's old residence to someone. Li Shidao, military governor of Pinglu, requested to redeem it with his private wealth.
