translations.idiomatic: Chou, a great-great-grandson of Wei Zheng, was extremely poor and had pawned the family's old residence. Li Shidao, military governor of Pinglu, requested to redeem it with his private wealth.

sentences.zh: 上命白居易草詔，居易奏言：「事關激勸，宜出朝廷。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Bai Juyi to draft an edict. Juyi submitted a memorial stating: "This affair concerns encouragement and reward; it should come from the court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Bai Juyi to draft an edict. Juyi submitted a memorial stating: "This affair concerns encouragement and reward; it should come from the court.

sentences.zh: 師道何人，敢掠斯美！

translations.literal: Who is Shidao, that he dares seize this honor for himself!
translations.idiomatic: Who is Li Shidao, that he dares seize this honor for himself!

sentences.zh: 望敕有司以官錢贖還後嗣。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order the responsible offices to redeem it with official funds and restore it to his descendants."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will order the responsible offices to redeem it with official funds and restore it to his descendants."

sentences.zh: 上從之，出内庫錢二千緡贖賜魏稠，仍禁質賣。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice, disbursing two thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury to redeem and bestow the property on Wei Chou, and also forbade pawning or selling it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed his advice, disbursing two thousand strings of cash from the inner treasury to redeem and bestow the property on Wei Chou, and also forbade pawning or selling it.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叔父士則以承宗擅自立，恐禍及宗，與幕客劉棲楚倶自歸京師。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong's uncle Shize, because Chengzong had enthroned himself without authorization, feared disaster would reach the clan and, together with his staff member Liu Qichu, voluntarily returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong's uncle Shize, fearing that Chengzong's unauthorized self-enthronement would bring disaster on the clan, returned to the capital together with his staff member Liu Qichu.

sentences.zh: 詔以士則爲神策大將軍。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Shize General of the Shence Army.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Shize General of the Shence Army.

sentences.zh: □翰林學士李絳等奏曰：「陛下嗣膺大寶，四年於茲，而儲闈未立，典冊不行，是開窺覦之端，乖重愼之義，非所以承宗廟、重社稷也。

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and others submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has succeeded to the Great Mandate, and four years have now passed, yet the heir apparent has not been established and the investiture rites have not been performed. This opens the way to covetous ambition and violates the principle of utmost caution. It is not the way to uphold the ancestral temple and honor the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang and others submitted a memorial, saying: "Your Majesty has succeeded to the Great Mandate, and four years have now passed, yet the heir apparent has not been established and the investiture rites have not been performed. This opens the way to covetous ambition and violates the principle of utmost caution. It is not the way to uphold the ancestral temple and honor the altars of soil and grain.

sentences.zh: 伏望抑手爲謙之小節，行至公之大典。」

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will restrain the small propriety of modest refusal and carry out the great rite of impartial public duty."
translations.idiomatic: We humbly hope Your Majesty will set aside the small propriety of modest refusal and carry out the great rite of impartial public duty."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，制立長子鄧王寧爲皇太子。

translations.literal: On the day dingmao, an edict was issued establishing the eldest son, Prince of Deng, Ning, as Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day, an edict was issued establishing the eldest son, Prince of Deng, Ning, as Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 寧，紀美人之子也。

translations.literal: Ning was the son of the Lady Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Ning was the son of the Lady Ji.

sentences.zh: 辛未，靈鹽節度使范希朝奏以太原防秋兵六百人衣糧給沙陀，許之。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, Fan Xichao, military governor of Ling and Salt, memorialized that six hundred autumn-defense troops from Taiyuan should be supplied with clothing and provisions for the Shatuo; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day, Fan Xichao, military governor of Ling and Salt, memorialized that six hundred autumn-defense troops from Taiyuan should be supplied with clothing and provisions for the Shatuo; this was approved.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，山南東道節度使裴均恃有中人之助，於德音後首進銀器千五百餘兩。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Pei Jun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, relying on the support of eunuchs, was the first after the benevolent edict to present more than fifteen hundred taels of silver vessels.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Pei Jun, military governor of Shannan East Circuit, relying on eunuch support, was the first after the benevolent edict to present more than fifteen hundred taels of silver vessels.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士李絳、白居易等上言：「均欲以此嘗陛下，願卻之。」

translations.literal: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang, Bai Juyi, and others submitted memorials: "Jun wishes to use this to test Your Majesty; we hope it will be refused."
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin academicians Li Jiang, Bai Juyi, and others submitted memorials: "Jun wishes to use this to test Your Majesty; we hope it will be refused."

sentences.zh: 上遽命出銀器付度支。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately ordered the silver vessels taken out and delivered to the Department of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor immediately ordered the silver vessels taken out and delivered to the Department of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 既而有旨諭進奏院：「自今諸道進奉，無得申御史台；

translations.literal: Soon afterward there was an order instructing the Memorial Submission Office: "From now on, when buffer regions make tribute offerings, they must not report them to the Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward there was an order instructing the Memorial Submission Office: "From now on, when buffer regions make tribute offerings, they must not report them to the Censorate;

sentences.zh: 有訪問者，輒以名聞。」

translations.literal: if anyone inquires, immediately report his name."
translations.idiomatic: if anyone inquires, immediately report his name."

sentences.zh: 白居易復以爲言，上不聽。

translations.literal: Bai Juyi again spoke on the matter, but the Emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Juyi again spoke on the matter, but the Emperor did not listen.

sentences.zh: 上欲革河北諸鎭世襲之弊，乘王士眞死，欲自朝廷除人，不從則興師討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to reform the evil of hereditary succession in the Hebei buffer regions. Taking advantage of Wang Shizhen's death, he wished to appoint someone from court; if they did not obey, he would raise an army to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to reform the evil of hereditary succession in the Hebei buffer regions. Taking advantage of Wang Shizhen's death, he planned to appoint someone from court; if they did not obey, he would raise an army to punish them.

sentences.zh: 裴垍曰：「李納跋扈不恭，王武俊有功於國，陛下前許師道，今奪承宗，沮勸違理，彼必不服。」

translations.literal: Pei Ji said: "Li Na is arrogant and disrespectful, while Wang Wujun rendered service to the state. Your Majesty previously granted Shidao's request; now to deprive Chengzong of succession discourages merit and violates reason—they will surely not submit."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ji said: "Li Na is arrogant and disrespectful, while Wang Wujun rendered service to the state. Your Majesty previously granted Li Shidao's request; now to deprive Chengzong of succession discourages merit and violates reason—they will surely not submit."

sentences.zh: 由是議久不決。

translations.literal: Because of this, deliberation long remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, deliberation long remained unresolved.

sentences.zh: 上以問諸學士，李絳等對曰：「河北不遵聲教，誰不憤歎，然今日取之，或恐未能。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked the academicians about it. Li Jiang and others replied: "Hebei does not obey the imperial teaching—who is not indignant and sighing? Yet to take it today, I fear, may not yet be possible.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked the academicians about it. Li Jiang and others replied: "Hebei does not obey the imperial teaching—who is not indignant? Yet to take it today, I fear, may not yet be possible.

sentences.zh: 成德軍自武俊以來，父子相承四十餘年，人情貫習，不以爲非。

translations.literal: The Chengde army, since Wujun's time, has passed father to son for more than forty years; custom has long acculturated the people, and they do not regard it as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The Chengde army has passed from father to son for more than forty years since Wang Wujun's time; custom has long acculturated the people, and they do not regard it as wrong.

sentences.zh: 況承宗已總軍務，一旦易之，恐未即奉詔。

translations.literal: Moreover, Chengzong already commands military affairs; to replace him at once, I fear, he will not immediately obey the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Chengzong already commands military affairs; to replace him at once, I fear, he will not immediately obey the edict.

sentences.zh: 又范陽、魏博、易定、淄靑以地相傳，與成德同體，彼聞成德除人，必内不自安，陰相黨助，雖茂昭有請，亦恐非誠。

translations.literal: Furthermore, Fanyang, Weibo, Yiding, and Ziqing pass their territories from hand to hand and share the same body with Chengde. When they hear that Chengde is to receive an appointee from court, they will surely be inwardly unsettled and secretly aid one another as a faction. Even if Maozhao has made a request, I fear it may not be sincere.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, Fanyang, Weibo, Yiding, and Ziqing pass their territories from hand to hand and share the same body with Chengde. When they hear that Chengde is to receive an appointee from court, they will surely be inwardly unsettled and secretly aid one another as a faction. Even if Maozhao has made a request, I fear it may not be sincere.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，今國家除人代承宗，彼鄰道勸成，進退有利。

translations.literal: The reason is this: if the state now appoints someone to replace Chengzong, the neighboring circuits can encourage success or failure, and profit either way.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is this: if the state now appoints someone to replace Chengzong, the neighboring circuits can encourage success or failure and profit either way.

sentences.zh: 若所除之人得入，彼則自以爲功；

translations.literal: If the appointee can enter, they will claim the credit for themselves;
translations.idiomatic: If the appointee can enter, they will claim the credit for themselves;

sentences.zh: 若詔令有所不行，彼因潛相交結，在於國體，豈可遽休！

translations.literal: if the edict is not obeyed, they will then secretly join together—in matters concerning the body of the state, how can this be quickly ended!
translations.idiomatic: if the edict is not obeyed, they will then secretly join together—in matters concerning the body of the state, how can this be quickly ended!

sentences.zh: 須興師四面攻討，彼將帥則加官爵，士卒則給衣糧，按兵玩寇，坐觀勝負，而勞費之病盡歸國家矣。

translations.literal: It would require raising armies on all four sides to attack and punish them. Their commanders would be given ranks and titles, their soldiers supplied with clothing and provisions; they would hold their troops and toy with the enemy, sitting by to watch the outcome—and the burden of toil and expense would all fall on the state.
translations.idiomatic: It would require raising armies on all four sides to attack and punish them. Their commanders would be given ranks and titles, their soldiers supplied with clothing and provisions; they would hold their troops and toy with the enemy, sitting by to watch the outcome—and the burden of toil and expense would all fall on the state.

sentences.zh: 今江、淮水，公私困竭，軍旅之事，殆未可輕議也。」

translations.literal: Now the Jiang and Huai regions have suffered floods, and public and private resources are exhausted; military affairs, I fear, should not be lightly discussed."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Jiang and Huai regions have suffered floods, and public and private resources are exhausted; military affairs, I fear, should not be lightly discussed."

sentences.zh: 左軍中尉吐突承璀欲希上意，奪裴垍權，自請將兵討之。

translations.literal: Tuote Chengcui, Left Army Commandant, wished to win the Emperor's favor, seize Pei Ji's authority, and volunteered to lead troops to punish Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuote Chengcui, Left Army Commandant, wished to win the Emperor's favor, seize Pei Ji's authority, and volunteered to lead troops to punish Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 上疑未決，宗正少卿李拭奏稱：「承宗不可不討。

translations.literal: The Emperor was doubtful and had not decided. Li Shi, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, submitted a memorial stating: "Chengzong must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was doubtful and had not decided. Li Shi, Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, submitted a memorial stating: "Chengzong must be punished.

sentences.zh: 承璀親近信臣，宜委以禁兵，使統諸軍，誰敢不服！」

translations.literal: Chengcui is a close and trusted minister; he should be entrusted with the palace guard and made to command all the armies—who would dare not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Chengcui is a close and trusted minister; he should be entrusted with the palace guard and made to command all the armies—who would dare not submit!"

sentences.zh: 上以拭狀示諸學士曰：「此奸臣也，知騰欲將承璀，故上此奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor showed Shi's memorial to the academicians and said: "This is a villainous minister. Knowing that I wish to put Chengcui in command, he submitted this memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed Shi's memorial to the academicians and said: "This is a villainous minister. Knowing that I wish to put Chengcui in command, he submitted this memorial.

sentences.zh: 卿曹記之，自今勿令得進用。」

translations.literal: You gentlemen take note of this—from now on, do not let him be promoted and employed."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen take note of this—from now on, do not let him be promoted and employed."

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使盧從史遭父喪，朝廷久未起復，從史懼，因承璀説上，請發本軍討承宗。

translations.literal: Lu Congshi, military governor of Zhaoyi, had suffered his father's death, and the court had long failed to grant him leave from mourning. Congshi was afraid and, through Chengcui, persuaded the Emperor to request that his own army be sent to punish Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Congshi, military governor of Zhaoyi, had suffered his father's death, and the court had long failed to grant him leave from mourning. Congshi was afraid and, through Chengcui, persuaded the Emperor to request that his own army be sent to punish Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，起復從史左金吾大將軍，餘如故。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Congshi was granted leave from mourning and made General of the Left Golden Guard; the rest of his duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On the renchen day, Congshi was granted leave from mourning and made General of the Left Golden Guard; the rest of his duties remained as before.

sentences.zh: 初，平涼之盟，副無帥判官路泌、會盟判官鄭叔矩皆沒於吐蕃。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the Pingliang alliance, Lu Bi, vice-commissioner and judge in the absence of the commander, and Zheng Shuju, alliance judge, were both captured by the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the Pingliang alliance, Lu Bi, vice-commissioner and judge in the absence of the commander, and Zheng Shuju, alliance judge, were both captured by the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 其後吐蕃請和，泌子隨三詣闕號泣上表，乞從其請。

translations.literal: Afterward the Tibetans requested peace. Bi's son Sui three times came to the palace gate, weeping and submitting memorials, begging that their request be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Tibetans requested peace. Bi's son Sui three times came to the palace gate, weeping and submitting memorials, begging that their request be granted.

sentences.zh: 德宗以吐蕃多詐，不許。

translations.literal: Dezong, considering the Tibetans deceitful, did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong, considering the Tibetans deceitful, did not grant it.

sentences.zh: 至是，吐蕃復請和，隨又五上表，詣執政泣請，裴垍、李籓亦言於上，請許其和。

translations.literal: At this time the Tibetans again requested peace. Sui submitted five more memorials and went to the chief ministers weeping and pleading; Pei Ji and Li Fan also spoke to the Emperor, requesting that peace be granted.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Tibetans again requested peace. Sui submitted five more memorials and went to the chief ministers weeping and pleading; Pei Ji and Li Fan also spoke to the Emperor, requesting that peace be granted.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed their advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed their advice.

sentences.zh: 五月，命祠部郎中徐復使吐蕃。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xu Fu of the Ministry of Rites was ordered as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xu Fu of the Ministry of Rites was sent as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 六月，以靈鹽節度使范希朝爲河東節度使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Fan Xichao, military governor of Ling-Salt, was made military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Fan Xichao was transferred from Ling-Salt to military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 朝議以沙陀在靈武，迫近吐蕃，慮其反覆，又部落衆多，恐長谷價，乃命悉從希朝詣河東。

translations.literal: At court it was argued that because the Shatuo were at Lingwu, close to Tibet, there was fear they might turn traitor; moreover their tribes were numerous and there was fear they would only grow in strength and expense—therefore an order was issued that they all follow Xichao to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that with the Shatuo at Lingwu, near Tibet, they might prove unreliable; their tribes were also numerous, and officials feared they would only grow stronger and costlier—so the whole group was ordered to move east with Xichao to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 希朝選其驍騎千二百，號沙陀軍，置使以領之，而處其餘衆於定襄川。

translations.literal: Xichao selected twelve hundred of their finest horsemen and styled them the Shatuo Army, appointing a commissioner to command them, while settling the remainder of the people at Dingsiang River.
translations.idiomatic: Xichao chose twelve hundred of their best horsemen as the Shatuo Army under a dedicated commander, and resettled the rest of the tribe along the Dingsiang River.

sentences.zh: 於是朱邪執宜始保神武川之黃花堆。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhuye Zhigong first held Huanghua Mound in the Shenwu River region.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Zhuye Zhigong made his base at Huanghua Mound on the Shenwu River.

sentences.zh: 左軍中尉吐突承璀領功德使，盛修安國寺，奏立聖德碑，髙大一准《華岳碑》，先構碑樓，請敕學士撰文，且言「臣已具錢萬緡，欲酬之。」

translations.literal: The Left Army Commandant Tuhu Chenghui held the post of merit commissioner and lavishly restored Anguo Temple. He memorialized to erect a stele of sagely virtue, its height to match the Hua Yue stele, first building a stele pavilion and asking that an edict order an academician to compose the text, adding, "Your servant has already prepared ten thousand strings of cash to pay for it."
translations.idiomatic: Left Army Commandant Tuhu Chenghui, as merit commissioner, lavishly rebuilt Anguo Temple and asked to erect a "stele of sagely virtue" as tall as the Hua Yue stele. He built the pavilion first and requested an imperial order for a scholar to write the inscription, adding that he had prepared ten thousand strings of cash as payment.

sentences.zh: 上命李絳爲之，絳上言：「堯、舜、禹、湯，未嘗立碑自言聖德，惟秦始皇於巡遊所過，刻石髙自稱述，未審陛下欲何所法！

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Li Jiang to write it. Jiang submitted: "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang never erected steles to proclaim their own sagely virtue. Only the First Emperor of Qin, wherever he passed on his tours, carved stones and loftily praised himself—may it be asked which model Your Majesty wishes to follow!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Li Jiang to compose the text. Jiang objected: "Yao, Shun, Yu, and Tang never set up steles boasting of their own virtue. Only the First Emperor of Qin carved self-praise on stone wherever he traveled—which precedent does Your Majesty mean to follow?

sentences.zh: 且敘修寺之美，不過壯麗觀游，豈所以光益聖德！」

translations.literal: Moreover, to narrate the beauty of restoring a temple is nothing more than magnifying a sight for touring—how could that be a means to enhance sagely virtue!"
translations.idiomatic: And praising the splendor of a temple restoration is merely glorifying a sightseeing attraction—how does that enhance your sacred virtue?"

sentences.zh: 上覽奏，承璀適在旁，上命曳倒碑樓。

translations.literal: When the Emperor read the memorial, Chenghui happened to be at his side. The Emperor ordered the stele pavilion dragged down.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor read the memorial, Chenghui happened to be present. The Emperor ordered the stele pavilion torn down at once.

sentences.zh: 承璀言：「碑樓甚大，不可曳，請徐毀撤。」

translations.literal: Chenghui said, "The stele pavilion is very large and cannot be dragged down. I beg that it be demolished gradually."
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui said, "The pavilion is too large to pull down. Please let it be dismantled slowly."

sentences.zh: 冀得延引，乘間再論。

translations.literal: He hoped to gain delay and seize an opening to argue again.
translations.idiomatic: He hoped to delay matters and find another chance to press his case.

sentences.zh: 上厲聲曰：「多用牛曳之！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said sharply, "Use many oxen to drag it down!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor snapped, "Use as many oxen as it takes—pull it down!"

sentences.zh: 承璀乃不敢言。

translations.literal: Chenghui then did not dare speak further.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghui dared say no more.

sentences.zh: 凡用百牛曳之，乃倒。

translations.literal: In all, a hundred oxen were used to drag it, and then it fell.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred oxen were hitched to it before the pavilion finally came down.
